claims.text: On the 4Q24 earnings call (period 2024-12-31, published 2025-01-16), CEO Ted Pick said Wealth Management's "investments in our self-directed and Workplace channels drive our differentiated client acquisition funnel," and that with its expanded offering the firm reaches "over 19 million relationships" and has added "net new assets of over $250 billion in each of the past two years."

On the 1Q25 earnings call (period 2025-03-31), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said fee-based flows were "again supported by assets migrating from advisor-led brokerage accounts to fee-based accounts" and by "assets migrating to the advisor-led channel that originated from the workplace channel," including "an incremental $20 billion this quarter, adding to the roughly $300 billion accumulated from workplace since we expanded our channel in 2020."

On the 2Q25 earnings call (period 2025-06-30), CEO Ted Pick described "ongoing investments in our world-class platform, including investments to support our advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and the expansion of our essential workplace channel" as "an engine for future growth."

On the 2Q25 earnings call (period 2025-06-30), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said "70% of the flows that come from workplace, that originate from workplace, is actually net new assets to the firm," describing it as "an incredible number" and evidence of "what we intended to see in the investments in workplace."

On the 3Q25 earnings call (period 2025-09-30), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said assets "that originated from workplace continue to migrate into our advisor-led channel as a result of the consistent investments we have made into our differentiated platform," and the firm continues "to invest, deepening our competitive moats in areas like our expanded collaboration with Carta in private markets and in digital assets through announced partnerships with Zero Hash."

On the 3Q25 earnings call (period 2025-09-30), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said the firm has been "increasing our marketing and business development" in self-directed, is "attracting assets held away" and "bringing in new clients... a lot of the tools that we've been giving to our advisors," while workplace "is bringing in assets not just in NNA, but also directly into fee-based flows."

On the 4Q25 earnings call (period 2025-12-31), CEO Ted Pick said "We continue to invest in each of our three business segments: Wealth, Institutional Securities, and Investment Management via human capital and technology," and that "The funnel is working," citing "$1.6 trillion plus of net new assets" over the last five years "with a doubling of fee-based flows."

On the 4Q25 earnings call (period 2025-12-31), management said "Advisor-led assets originating from workplace and E*TRADE relationships accelerated, growing to a record $99 billion for the full year, compared to historical averages of around $60 billion per year," and that "Workplace and E-Trade relationships continue to seek out advice."

On the 1Q26 earnings call (period 2026-03-31), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said household penetration of lending products "is now at 18%... up from 14% just 5 years ago through ongoing investments in technology, adviser and client education, and an expanded product set."

On the 2Q26 earnings call (period 2026-06-30), CFO Sharon Yeshaya described "the workplace channel as a strong contributor to the top of the funnel," saying "Workplace brings relationships and assets onto the platform" and "Our investments are extending our runway for growth," including continuing to "deliver advice and solutions to new and existing relationships, supporting the build in our fee-based assets."

On the 2Q26 earnings call (period 2026-06-30), CEO Ted Pick said "Growth led by workplace relationships reflects a cornerstone of our client acquisition funnel" and "Our ability to serve clients across the private to public continuum continues to attract assets to our world-class platform."

On the 2Q26 earnings call (period 2026-06-30), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said "The execution of our strategy, particularly our sustained investments in our client acquisition funnel allowed us to reach more clients and deepen existing relationships."

On the 3Q26 earnings call (period 2026-09-30), CEO Ted Pick said the E*TRADE acquisition "completed the funnel," describing it as "this extraordinary self-directed piece, the workplace and then, of course, the financial adviser."
On the 3Q26 earnings call (period 2026-09-30), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said "our pipeline and our connectivity across channels allows us to build relationships early and deepen them over time."

claims.text: On the 2025-09-30 earnings call (published 2025-10-22), CEO Paul Shoukry described Raymond James's 'best-of-both-worlds value proposition, where we offer a unique combination of an advisor and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions,' adding that its 'strong balance sheet and commitment to independence is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.'

On the 2025-06-30 earnings call (published 2025-07-23), management said its 'best of both worlds value proposition... continues to resonate with advisors across all of our affiliation options,' and cited its 'strong balance sheet and commitment to independence' as 'increasingly becoming a differentiator.'

The 2025 10-K (period 2025-09-30) states Raymond James offers 'multiple affiliation options, which we refer to as AdvisorChoice®,' where financial advisors affiliate as employees, independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers through its RIA and Custody Services division.

Raymond James's affiliation-options recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) frames the pitch as 'The Power of Choice,' listing Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA options, 'all backed by the full support of a leading independent financial firm.'

claims.text: Raymond James's Traditional Employee Advisor recruiting page (page content as of 2026-05-16) states 'Book ownership is just the beginning' and promises 'no quotas, no product pushing' along with 'compelling practice resources, purpose-made technology and a powerful investment platform.'

claims.text: Raymond James's Advisor Select® recruiting page (page content as of 2026-03-11) describes Advisor Select as 'an employee affiliation option for advisors who want to lead a team,' providing 'the full benefits of our employee channel with the independence to create their own branches.'

The 2025 Investor Day deck (published 2025-06-05) states the AdvisorChoice spectrum 'services the largest addressable market in the industry,' spanning employee, independent contractor, and RIA & custody services, and notes 'the movement to independence is not channel-specific.'

On the 2025-12-31 earnings call (published 2026-01-28), management said advisor satisfaction 'is at the highest it's been since, I think, 2014,' and pointed to advisor book ownership plus 'close to $1.1 billion' of technology investment as differentiators.

claims.text: On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), CEO Rick Wurster said that in Schwab's advisor services business it launched Advisor ProDirect, 'a fee-based, membership-driven offer designed to support independence for new RIAs.'

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab's four strategic focus areas are growth, scale and efficiency, 'the brilliant basics,' and its people, and that in advisor services Schwab is 'deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms we serve by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs'; he cited grown lending support, alternatives capability, and an expanded institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform including funds from nearly 60 managers, as well as the launch of Advisor ProDirect to help breakaway advisors on their path to independence.

On the 4Q25 Winter Business Update call (January 2026), CEO Rick Wurster said that in Advisor Services Schwab is attracting net new assets from new and existing advisors of all sizes and that, 'No matter an RIA size, we serve them all in a way no competitor can.'

On the 4Q25 Winter Business Update call (January 2026), CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab is 'winning across every dimension' in Advisor Services, citing its size, scale, and the breadth and strength of its capabilities, a custody offering it continues to make 'better, easier, and more straightforward for advisors,' the consulting and advice and expertise it brings, and support for advisors' drive to independence; he said Schwab grew that business '6.5% organically last year or roughly around that level.'

The 2025 10-K states that through the Advisor Services segment Schwab has become one of the largest providers of custodial, trading, banking, and support services to RIAs and their clients, and that management believes it can maintain its competitive position primarily through its sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams 'dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed in serving their clients.'

The 2025 10-K states that in addition to focusing on superior service, Schwab utilizes technology to provide RIAs with a 'highly-developed, scalable platform for administering their clients' assets easily and efficiently,' and that Advisor Services sponsors and hosts national, regional, local, and virtual events designed to help RIAs of all sizes and complexities expand and efficiently manage their practices.

The 2025 10-K states that by functioning as custodian, Schwab earns revenue associated with the underlying client assets, predominantly through net interest revenue and asset management and administration fees, and that 'we do not charge the RIA or end client a custody fee.'

The 2025 10-K states that Schwab provides extensive educational materials, programs, and events to RIAs, conducts industry research on an ongoing basis, sponsors and hosts the annual IMPACT® conference, and holds smaller events across the country each year; RIAs and their clients also have access to Schwab's broad range of wealth services including securities, mutual funds, ETFs, alternative investments, fixed income products, managed accounts, cash products, bank lending, and trust services.

The 2025 10-K states that in the Advisor Services arena Schwab competes with institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks, and trust companies.

The 2025 10-K describes Schwab's strategy as based on the principle that developing trusted relationships will translate into more assets from both new and existing clients, ultimately driving more revenue, and—along with expense discipline and thoughtful capital management—will generate earnings growth and build long-term stockholder value; it identifies scale and size of the business as a key competitive advantage, allowing Schwab to spread operating costs and amortize new investments over a large base of clients.

On the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026), CEO Rick Wurster said that in Advisor Services Schwab is continuing to enhance its digital experiences across RIA workflows like move money, account open, and account maintenance while modernizing tools on its adviser platform, helping RIAs get routine work done faster and with fewer errors.

Schwab's May 2026 investor day deck describes 'The leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, providing wealth tools, investment / lending products, & technology in addition to custody & service.'
Schwab's 2Q26 earnings deck (July 2026) lists 'RIA Support' among its select ongoing investments.
Schwab's 2Q26 earnings deck (July 2026) states 'Schwab remains the trusted platform of choice for investors & RIAs' and shows Schwab ranked #1 with $5.7 trillion in RIA custodial assets.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), CEO Rick Wurster said, 'We have built our adviser business around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed,' and that Schwab serves more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets with a platform bringing together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology, and dedicated service and support; he said this business requires scale, trust, operational excellence, outstanding service, and breadth.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), CEO Rick Wurster said advisers of all sizes are turning to Schwab, that last year more than 1,100 advisory firms added Schwab as a custodian—more than 3x the number of the next closest provider—and that Schwab is continuing to invest in this business to meet advisers' needs.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab's Client Promoter Scores have never been higher, the surveyed intent among adviser clients to bring new assets to Schwab has never been higher, and the ease of doing business for advisers at Schwab has never been higher, which is why 'we are the preferred custodian for most RIAs in the industry.'
Schwab's 3Q26 press release (October 15, 2026) states that Schwab 'Partnered with Anthropic to bring Claude for Financial Advisors directly to the independent RIAs Schwab serves.'

In an August 26, 2026 WealthManagement.com article, a Schwab spokesperson said that as the largest custodian for advisors, 'Schwab is focused on creating long-term value and access for advisors and retail investors,' and that 'we remain focused on investing in innovation, capabilities, and service to help advisors grow and investors succeed.'

WealthManagement.com reported on October 15, 2026 that CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab was the first RIA custodian included in Anthropic's Claude for Financial Advisors, an AI tool offering notetaking assistance, alternative investment briefings, compliance and policy reviews, and estate and tax briefings, and that the firm is working on a proprietary long-short investment strategy it will update on soon.

WealthManagement.com reported on October 15, 2026 that, according to Schwab, the firm added 1,001 new RIAs to its custody platform in Q3, with its nearest peers adding 349, 339, 202, and 79 respectively, and that the largest cohort of those joiners (36%) had AUM above $5 billion.

At Schwab Impact, as reported by WealthManagement.com on October 28, 2026, CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab will continue to focus on its custody services for registered investment advisors with under $100 million AUM, and stated, 'Our job and our role is to provide a platform and a support ecosystem that helps you support your clients and helps your firm thrive.'

WealthManagement.com reported on October 28, 2026 that Schwab made its Claude for Financial Advisors partnership available through Schwab Advisor Center and is offering a $4,800 credit for the enterprise version 'with the goal of giving smaller advisors access,' according to executives at Schwab Impact.

WealthManagement.com reported on October 29, 2026 that CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab wants to give registered investment advisors equal or better access than their wirehouse counterparts to banking services such as lending, private market investing, and long-short investment strategies, and that Schwab is 'increasingly trying to play a role of being their bank and helping them manage both sides of the balance sheet for their clients.'

claims.text: On the 2Q25 earnings call (June 2025), CFO Alastair Borthwick said Merrill and the Private Bank "continued to add financial advisors to the sales force in Merrill and the Private Bank through our extensive training program and experienced hiring of advisors," and that approximately one-third of net new households in Q2 were added by newly trained advisors.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (December 2025), Borthwick said "we're picking up the recruiting of experienced advisors," while describing experienced recruiting as not "an enormous part of our strategy" and saying the training program is "ultimately what we believe we can just keep driving in order to improve the net new flows."

claims.text: The 2025 10-K (fiscal year ended September 30, 2025) describes Raymond James's affiliation options as "multiple affiliation options, which we refer to as AdvisorChoice®": financial advisors affiliate directly as employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through the firm's RIA and Custody Services ("RCS") division.

The 2025 10-K states that employee financial advisors "work in a traditional branch," are compensated primarily through "a payout on revenues they generate," and participate in the firm's employee benefit plans.

The 2025 10-K states that independent contractor financial advisors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and, accordingly, receive a higher payout percentage than employee advisors; these options are designed to help advisors build their businesses with as much or as little of the firm's support as they determine, and such advisors may affiliate directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in the Financial Institutions Division.

The 2025 10-K describes the RCS division as offering third-party RIAs and broker-dealers a range of products and services including custodial services, trade execution, research, and other support, for fees that may be either transactional or based on AUA.

Raymond James's affiliation-options recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) presents AdvisorChoice® as "The Power of Choice," saying advisors can match their professional goals to the affiliation option that is right for them, and lists Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: The recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) publishes payout ranges for three models: Traditional Employee "Up to 50% payout" plus employee benefits; Advisor Select "70-80% gross payout" plus employee benefits; Independent Contractor "81% to 90% payout."
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: The recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) also describes Bank & Credit Union (a compensation package from the financial institution in partnership with Raymond James), Corporate RIA ("81% to 90% payout"), and RIA & Custody Services (compensation determined with the RIA or broker-dealer, with the advisor responsible for compliance).
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: The June 5, 2025 Investor Day deck states that the AdvisorChoice spectrum "services the largest addressable market in the industry," spanning employee, independent contractor, and RIA & Custody Services, and adds that "The movement to 'independence' is not channel-specific."

On the fiscal first-quarter 2026 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), CEO Paul Shoukry said Raymond James has "the largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody, and we have critical mass and decades of experience in all of them."

On the fiscal third-quarter 2026 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said "strong retention and continued recruiting momentum again demonstrated that Raymond James remains a destination of choice for financial advisers across our affiliation options."

The 2025 10-K reports financial advisor counts by affiliation: as of September 30, 2023, 3,693 employees and 5,019 independent contractors (8,712 total); as of September 30, 2024, 3,826 employees and 4,961 independent contractors (8,787 total); as of September 30, 2025, 3,878 employees and 5,065 independent contractors (8,943 total).
The 2025 10-K states that financial advisors associated with firms in RCS are not included in Raymond James's financial advisor counts, although their client assets are included in the firm's AUA.

On the fiscal fourth-quarter 2024 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2024), then-CEO Paul Reilly said that in the RIA part (RCS) "it is by far the highest percentage growth," while in total dollars "this year, the employee channel really led the way"; a couple of years ago it was the independent channel, and he said the firm no longer sees the pattern of independents growing faster in down markets and employees in up markets.

On the fiscal third-quarter 2025 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2025), CEO Paul Shoukry said "the acceleration rate within the independent channel is probably higher, but we are still seeing very good success in the employee affiliation option and the independent RIA option as well."

On the fiscal fourth-quarter 2025 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), CEO Paul Shoukry said Raymond James "ended the fiscal year with a record number of financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year."

On the fiscal first-quarter 2026 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), CEO Paul Shoukry said recruiting "is broad-based across our affiliation options, maybe more heavily tilted in the last six months on the independent contractor side of the business."

On the fiscal second-quarter 2026 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said "over the last year, in particular, much more of our recruiting has come from the independent side of the business versus the employee side of the business," a mix shift that affects the compensation ratio because independent payouts are higher to cover advisors' overhead costs.

On the same fiscal second-quarter 2026 call, CEO Paul Shoukry added "we're actually seeing pretty good uptick in the employee affiliation option as well" and "really good momentum across all affiliation options," with the employee side "continues to tick up."

The June 5, 2025 Investor Day deck shows domestic PCG assets under administration by affiliation model from March 31, 2020 to March 31, 2025: Employee $332 billion to $631 billion; Independent contractor $318 billion to $543 billion; RIA & Custody Services $46 billion to $186 billion; total $696 billion to $1,360 billion. The deck also lists 5-year CAGRs of 32%, 11%, 14% and 14%.

Raymond James's 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2025 reports RCS client assets included in PCG AUA of $201.6 billion (June 30, 2025), $185.6 billion (March 31, 2025) and $167.2 billion (June 30, 2024).
The 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2025 reports RCS client assets of $224.6 billion (December 31, 2025), $217.3 billion (September 30, 2025) and $188.2 billion (December 31, 2024).
The 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 reports RCS client assets of $228.2 billion (March 31, 2026), $224.6 billion (December 31, 2025) and $185.6 billion (March 31, 2025).

The 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 reports RCS client assets of $251.3 billion (June 30, 2026), $228.2 billion (March 31, 2026) and $201.6 billion (June 30, 2025), of which $220.1 billion were assets in fee-based accounts at June 30, 2026.

The 2025 10-K states that RCS division services are provided for fees that may be either transactional or based on AUA, and that firms affiliated through RCS retain the fees they charge to their clients and are generally responsible for all of their direct costs.
The 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 states that revenues related to RCS assets in the PCG segment are included in "Account and service fees."
The 2025 10-K reports PCG segment net revenues of $10.18 billion for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025, without breaking them out by affiliation model.

The 2025 10-K risk factors state that the PCG business faces risks from the "continued industry-wide trend in which financial advisors are departing traditional firms, including to form independent RIAs or to join existing third-party RIAs, some of which are backed by private equity investors," and that the firm seeks to mitigate these risks through financial advisor succession planning and support resources.

Raymond James's 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 states that the growth in RCS client assets "is partially due to transfers into RCS from our other financial advisor channels," and that while the firm may continue to experience such transfers, it "would not expect these financial advisor transfers to significantly impact our results of operations."

On the fiscal fourth-quarter 2024 earnings call, then-CEO Paul Reilly said RCS has "by far the highest percentage growth" among the affiliation options, while in total dollars the employee channel led that year, and that the firm no longer sees a market-dependent split between independent and employee growth.

On the fiscal third-quarter 2025 earnings call, CEO Paul Shoukry said there have been "M&A-driven catalysts, particularly on the independent side of the business," which "contributed to the acceleration in our recruiting pipeline," while success is not concentrated from that one catalyst alone.

On the fiscal second-quarter 2026 earnings call, CEO Paul Shoukry described the recent recruiting mix shift toward the independent side, while also saying the employee affiliation option "continues to tick up" and that there is "really good momentum across all affiliation options."

On the fiscal third-quarter 2026 earnings call, CEO Paul Shoukry said the recruiting pipeline "is not a pipeline that is driven by one firm or one catalyst in the market or one affiliation option," but is "broad-based" across the variety of affiliation options.

WealthManagement.com (October 29, 2026) reported that, according to CEO Paul Shoukry, the independent contractor channel "is seeing the most interest in terms of dollar volume," while "the RIA custody division on a smaller base is growing at a high percentage rate as well."

WealthManagement.com (October 8, 2026) reported that four practices with more than $1 billion in client assets joined Ascentis Independent Advisors from Raymond James Financial Services, and that the practices would continue to use Raymond James as their primary custodian.

WealthManagement.com (October 27, 2026) reported that a Georgia-based team with about $1.1 billion in client assets left Raymond James Financial Services to become an independent RIA, custodying with Fidelity.

claims.text: Tier labels - Morgan Stanley: In its March 2026 Form 10-Q (period 2026-03-31), Morgan Stanley describes its Wealth Management clients as "individual investors, including high and ultra-high net worth individuals, and businesses and institutions," using "high" and "ultra-high net worth" as its wealth labels rather than a published tier ladder.

Tier labels - Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), CEO Edward Pick said Morgan Stanley clients have access to "ultra-high net worth family office infrastructure solutions," continuing the firm's use of "ultra-high net worth" as a label.

Tier labels - Merrill: The 2025 10-K (February 2026) states Bank of America Private Bank, together with Merrill Wealth Management's Private Wealth Management business, provides solutions "targeted to high net worth and ultra high net worth clients."

Tier labels - Merrill: WealthManagement.com trade press (October 2026) quoted Merrill Co-Head Lindsay Hans saying year-over-year percentage increases for clients in the "$1 million and $10 million-plus segments" were in the double digits, indicating Merrill's higher client tiers.
Asset or net worth thresholds - Merrill: In its November 2025 investor-day deck, Merrill reports "750K $500K+ households" and "54K $10MM+ households."

Asset or net worth thresholds - Merrill: The 2025 10-K (February 2026) states Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business provides a high-touch experience through a network of financial advisors "focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets."
Asset or net worth thresholds - Merrill: On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), CFO Alastair Borthwick said Merrill added "about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets."

Criteria disclosed - Morgan Stanley: The March 2026 Form 10-Q (period 2026-03-31) states Wealth Management "supports clients through three channels: Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace," and the 3Q26 supplement (October 2026) defines self-directed client assets as active accounts "having at least $25 in assets" that are not advisor-led, so the firm segments reporting by service channel rather than by published wealth tier.

Criteria disclosed - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (February 2026) describes Wealth Management lending to "high to ultra-high net worth individuals," including "tailored lending to ultra-high net worth clients," using wealth labels as client descriptors without disclosing tier thresholds.

Criteria disclosed - Merrill: The 2025 10-K (February 2026) states Merrill Wealth Management "provides tailored solutions to meet clients' needs through a full set of investment management, brokerage, banking and retirement products," and that its Private Wealth Management business, with Bank of America Private Bank, provides customized solutions for clients' "wealth structuring, investment management, trust and banking needs."

claims.text: Definition and metric name - Morgan Stanley: The MS Wealth Management supplement (period 2020-12-31, published 2021-01-20) reports advisor headcount as a 'Wealth Management representatives' line under the advisor-led channel, and its end notes define advisor-led relationships by reference to assigned representatives: 'Advisor-led client assets represents client assets in accounts that have a Wealth Management representative assigned' [MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1][MS-SUPP-2020Q4#3]. The 3Q26 supplement (period 2026-09-30, published 2026-10-14) repeats that advisor-led client assets are 'client assets in accounts that have a Wealth Management representative assigned' [MS-SUPP-2026Q3#38].
claims.source_label: MS supplement 2020-12-31 [IR]; MS supplement - Wealth Management segment 2020-12-31 [IR]; MS supplement 2026-09-30, p.15 [IR]

claims.text: Definition and metric name - Schwab: Schwab's 3Q26 earnings deck abbreviations (period 2026-09-30, published 2026-10-15) define 'FC = Financial consultant' and 'WA = Wealth advisor' [SCHW-DECK-2026Q3#73]. Schwab does not publish a single advisor headcount metric in the evidence provided; its 10-Q references 'financial consultants and wealth advisors' within headcount [SCHW-10Q-2026Q2#25], and its 2025 10-K describes Schwab Wealth Advisory as providing 'a dedicated Wealth Advisor supported by a team of professionals' [SCHW-10K-2025#19].
claims.source_label: SCHW deck 2026-09-30, p.40 [IR]; SCHW 10-Q 2026-06-30 [filing]; SCHW 10-K - Investor Services segment 2025-12-31 [filing]

claims.text: Definition and metric name - Edward Jones: Edward Jones names the metric 'Financial advisors (actual),' reported as 'At period end' and 'Average' (10-Q, period 2026-06-26, published 2026-08-07) [EDJ-10Q-2026Q2#60]; the 10-K reports the same 'Financial advisors' metric at year end and average (period 2025-12-31, published 2026-03-13) [EDJ-10K-2025#142].

Definition and metric name - Merrill: Merrill's advisory business is described in BAC's 2025 10-K (segment GWIM, published 2026-02-25) as providing 'a high-touch client experience through a network of financial advisors focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets' [BAC-10K-2025#246]. Merrill does not report a standalone advisor headcount metric.

Definition and metric name - Raymond James: Raymond James's 2025 10-K refers to its 'financial advisor counts' and 'financial advisor metric' [RJF-10K-2025#12][RJF-10K-2025#228]; on the 4Q25 earnings call (period 2025-09-30, published 2025-10-22) management cited 'a record number of financial advisors of 8,943' [RJF-TR-2025Q3#4].
claims.source_label: RJF 10-K - Private Client Group segment 2025-09-30 [filing]; RJF 10-K 2025-09-30 [filing]; RJF transcript 2025-09-30 [IR]

claims.text: Reporting location and method - Morgan Stanley: MS discloses the 'Wealth Management representatives' figure in its quarterly Wealth Management Financial Information and Statistical Data supplement (e.g., 15,950 at Dec 31, 2020) [MS-SUPP-2020Q4#1].

Reporting location and method - Schwab: Schwab reports advisor hiring/growth qualitatively in 10-Q MD&A expense discussions — 'growth in headcount, including financial consultants and wealth advisors' (period 2026-06-30, published 2026-08-07) [SCHW-10Q-2026Q2#25] — and on earnings calls — 'We're continuing to hire financial consultants and wealth advisers' (period 2026-03-31, published 2026-04-16) [SCHW-TR-2026Q1#4].

Reporting location and method - Edward Jones: Edward Jones discloses financial advisor headcount in the 'Related metrics (actual)' tables of its 10-K/10-Q MD&A, split into U.S. and Canada columns (10-Q, period 2026-06-26, published 2026-08-07) [EDJ-10Q-2026Q2#82]; annual year-end and average figures appear in 10-K Item 7 (period 2025-12-31, published 2026-03-13) [EDJ-10K-2025#142].

Reporting location and method - Raymond James: Raymond James discloses its financial advisor count in the 10-K (Item 1 and Item 7, period 2025-09-30, published 2025-11-25) — including that the number increased year-over-year as recruits and trainees moving into production roles exceeded departures and planned retirements [RJF-10K-2025#228] — and on earnings calls ('record number of financial advisors of 8,943,' period 2025-09-30, published 2025-10-22) [RJF-TR-2025Q3#4].

Included roles - Morgan Stanley: MS counts as advisor-led the accounts 'that have a Wealth Management representative assigned' (3Q26 supplement, period 2026-09-30, published 2026-10-14) [MS-SUPP-2026Q3#38]; the January 2026 strategic-update deck builds 'Advisor-Led Households' from these advisor-led client assets [MS-DECK-2026-strategic-update#31].
claims.source_label: MS supplement 2026-09-30, p.15 [IR]; MS deck 2026-01-15, p.19 [IR]

claims.text: Included roles - Schwab: Schwab includes 'financial consultants' and 'wealth advisors' in its headcount and hiring references (10-Q, period 2026-06-30, published 2026-08-07) [SCHW-10Q-2026Q2#25]; Schwab Wealth Advisory provides 'a dedicated Wealth Advisor supported by a team of professionals' (2025 10-K) [SCHW-10K-2025#19].

claims.text: Included roles - Raymond James: Raymond James counts financial advisors who 'affiliate with us directly as either employees or independent contractors' (2025 10-K, Item 1, published 2025-11-25) [RJF-10K-2025#10]; its AdvisorChoice recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) lists Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA options [RJF-PR-web-affiliation-options#0], and management cited recruiting 'to our domestic independent contractor and employee channels' (3Q26 call, period 2026-06-30) [RJF-TR-2026Q2#5].
claims.source_label: RJF 10-K - Private Client Group segment 2025-09-30 [filing]; RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]; RJF transcript 2026-06-30 [IR]

claims.text: Excluded roles - Morgan Stanley: MS excludes self-directed accounts from the advisor-led count — 'Self-directed client assets represent active accounts which are not advisor led' (2025 10-K, period 2025-12-31) [MS-10K-2025#168]; workplace participants are a separate channel count, and 'individual households or participants that are engaged in one or more of our Wealth Management channels are included in each of the respective channel counts' [MS-10K-2025#168][MS-SUPP-2020Q4#3].
claims.source_label: MS 10-K - Wealth Management segment 2025-12-31 [filing]; MS supplement - Wealth Management segment 2020-12-31 [IR]

(2026 investor day deck, published 2026-05-14) [SCHW-DECK-2026-investor-day#306]; independent RIAs Schwab serves (more than 16,000 firms) are custodial clients, not Schwab advisors (3Q26 call, period 2026-09-30) [SCHW-TR-2026Q3#10].

Excluded roles - Edward Jones: Edward Jones reports 'Client support team professionals' and 'Home office associates' separately from financial advisors, and counts home office associates 'on a full-time equivalent basis' (10-Q, period 2025-06-27, published 2025-08-08) [EDJ-10Q-2025Q2#80][EDJ-10Q-2025Q2#81]; the 10-K describes CSTPs and home office associates as those 'who support those financial advisors' (period 2025-12-31) [EDJ-10K-2025#70].

claims.text: The 2025 10-K (Item 1) identifies "Scale and Size of the Business" as a key competitive advantage: "As one of the largest investment services firms in the U.S., we are able to spread operating costs and amortize new investments over a large base of clients, and harness the resources to evolve capabilities to meet client needs."

The 2025 10-K (Item 1) also cites "Operating Efficiency" — "Coupled with scale, our operating efficiency and sharing of infrastructure across different businesses creates a cost advantage that enables us to competitively price products and services while profitably serving clients of various sizes across multiple channels" — plus "Brand and Corporate Reputation" (which "enable[s] us to attract clients and employees"), "Service Culture" (which "increases the likelihood that those clients will refer others"), and "Willingness to Disrupt" (which "helps to attract more clients and assets").

On the Winter Business Update call (January 2026), CFO Mike Verdeschi said Schwab's spending plan drives "new client growth" by "investing in branches, adding more financial consultants and wealth advisors, advertising and marketing, expanding our digital asset offering to include spot crypto trading, and incorporating more AI across the firm."

On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab continues to invest to support growth "with more branches in local communities, more financial consultants, strategic marketing and advertising, including adapting our marketing to the increased influence of LLMs, the build-out of an RIA support ecosystem, and investments in bringing the breadth of Schwab to our workplace clients."

On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab's scale and efficiency efforts aim to "keep our structural cost advantage" and "keep our cost to serve low," creating "capacity to reinvest in the technology and capabilities."

The 3Q26 investor deck (October 2026) states Schwab's approach includes "Simplify & automate work," "faster, simpler & more digital experiences," and "Leverage our scale to maintain a structural cost advantage while continuing to invest in growth"; it reports 90% of accounts were opened digitally, 82% first call resolution, ~10% increase in FC meeting capacity, and 30-second average speed to answer.

The 2025 10-K (Item 1) states the scale advantage in cost terms: "As one of the largest investment services firms in the U.S., we are able to spread operating costs and amortize new investments over a large base of clients."

On the 1Q25 earnings call (April 2025), CFO Mike Verdeschi said Schwab has driven "expense on client assets down into the low double digits and improve[d] cost per account by more than 20% over the last decade."
The 2Q26 investor deck (July 2026) shows Schwab's cost per client account fell from $442 (GAAP) and $404 (adjusted) in 2020 to $332 (GAAP) and $319 (adjusted) in 2025, a -21% change.
The 2025 10-K (Item 7) states that "Total expenses excluding interest as a percentage of average client assets is a measure of operating efficiency" used by management.

In the 2Q26 press release (July 2026), CFO Mike Verdeschi attributed results partly to "the strength of Schwab's diversified business model, our industry-leading scale, and opportunistic capital return in multiple forms," delivering 43% year-over-year GAAP earnings growth.

On the Winter Business Update call (January 2026), CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab attracted $519 billion in core net new assets in 2025 (up 42% year over year) and clients opened 4.7 million new brokerage accounts (up 13%).

The 2025 10-K (Item 7) reports 2025 core net new assets of $519.4 billion (up 42%), an annualized organic growth rate of 5.1%, 4.7 million new brokerage accounts (up 13%), and 38.5 million active brokerage accounts at year-end 2025 (up 6%).
On the Winter Business Update call (January 2026), CEO Rick Wurster said 1.9 million new retail households turned to Schwab in 2025.

The 3Q26 press release (October 2026) reports core net new assets of $190.4 billion (up 38% versus 3Q25) and 1.2 million new brokerage account openings, bringing total client accounts to 48.6 million.
The 3Q26 investor deck (October 2026) reports 2026 year-to-date core net new assets of $450 billion (up 27% versus 2025 YTD) and 3.9 million new brokerage accounts (up 15%).

The 2Q26 10-Q states Edward Jones's more than 20,000 financial advisors serve more than 9 million clients with a total of $2.6 trillion in client assets under care as of June 26, 2026, supported by "approximately 55,000 associates and our branch presence in 68% of U.S. counties and all Canadian provinces."
The 2Q26 10-Q reports Edward Jones's net new assets increased 6% compared to the second quarter of 2025, and the Partnership ended the quarter with 20,514 financial advisors.

The 2Q25 10-Q reports Edward Jones's net new assets decreased 10% compared to the second quarter of 2024, "continuing a downward trend which can be attributed to higher asset outflows... including, without limitation, an aging client base and generational wealth transfers outside the firm, macroeconomic volatility, inflation and consumer spending."

The 3Q25 10-Q reports Edward Jones's net new assets increased 6% compared to the third quarter of 2024, and financial advisor attrition was 6.1% "as a result of a variety of factors, including a rise in financial advisor departures with tenure of five years or less."

The 2025 10-K (Item 1) states competing firms continue trying to hire away Edward Jones's financial advisors, "although the Partnership believes its rate of attrition of financial advisors is in line with comparable firms."

The 2025 10-K (Item 7) notes that inflation's impact on operating expenses "may affect profitability to the extent that additional costs are not recovered through attracting new clients, gathering new assets or raising prices of services."

The 2Q25 10-Q defines Edward Jones's "net new households" metric as "new client households opened less client households closed during the period, rounded to the nearest thousand," estimated based on available information.

The 2025 10-K (Item 1A) discloses Edward Jones initiatives "targeting new clients," including High Net Worth, Workplace, and "a new digital platform, focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors," as well as Financial Planning Services; it cautions that success depends on broad adoption by financial advisors, CSTPs and home office associates and that the timing or outcome cannot be reliably predicted.

The 2025 10-K (Item 1A) describes competitive pressure from "lower cost, computer-based 'robo-advice'" and "enhanced digital experiences," and says industry evolution has resulted, and is expected to continue to result, in "significant investments in financial advisors and other human capital, technology infrastructure, digital initiatives, knowledge- and data-powered tools, and strategic relationships."

The 2025 10-K (Item 1) states Edward Jones competes with "firms of all sizes offering discount services, usually with lower levels of personalized service to individual clients, including major competitor brokerage firms that offer zero commissions" and with "fintech" companies with internet- and mobile-based platforms; it also notes some competitors are "larger than the Partnership in terms of capital, resources, assets under care... and broader product offerings."

InvestmentNews trade press (August 2026) reports Edward Jones took a minority stake in Quicken, "a step towards integrating Quicken's personal financial management capabilities more directly into Edward Jones"; it also reports Edward Jones is "still determining the actual deployment strategy" for where or how Quicken will be offered to clients and integrated into its advisor software.

WealthManagement.com trade press (September 2026) reports Edward Jones is partnering with Aboon and Retirement Plan Advisory Group on an end-to-end retirement plan management tool covering "the entire workplace retirement plan lifecycle, from prospecting to plan servicing"; the prospecting module is in beta and expected to go live to the broader advisor network early next year.

The 2Q26 10-Q reports Edward Jones's communications and data processing expense increased "due to continued investments in new tools and technology and related higher depreciation expense as a result of these recent investments."

The evidence above only provides objective context for the strategic question asked. Whether or how Edward Jones should act is a judgment for the strategy team to make, beyond the scope of this evidence engine.

claims.text: The 2025 10-K states that Morgan Stanley's Wealth Management segment supports clients through three channels — Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace — and includes 'workplace services, including stock plan administration' and 'retirement plan services.'

The January 2026 strategic update deck defines 'Retirement and Financial Wellness Participants' as 'participants of corporate clients with financial wellness and retirement plans serviced by Morgan Stanley at Work,' and defines 'Advisor-Led Flows from Workplace and E*TRADE' as 'assets brought into advisor-led relationships, where the initial account was workplace or self-directed.'

The January 2026 strategic update deck positions 'Financial Wellness and Employee Benefits' as an early-stage offering to founders and employees to 'Invest for the Future,' alongside 'Founders Wealth Strategies.'

On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said that for workplace clients who 'might not yet have the advice-based relationship, we're working on that referral model,' which 'can begin as early as the financial education spot,' citing 'examples with 401(k)s and new 401(k) assets' where Morgan Stanley is 'giving people that ability to better understand where they could use advice.'
The 3Q26 earnings release (October 2026) states that Wealth Management fee-based flows of $80 billion 'included a new corporate retirement mandate.'
The 2025 10-K states that Morgan Stanley's workplace channel 'includes equity compensation solutions for companies, their executives and employees.'

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), CEO Ted Pick said Morgan Stanley at Work, 'with its exclusive partnership with Carta, positions us as an early trusted advisor to over 50,000 private companies,' and that 'employees across our workplace companies benefit from our management of equity compensation plans, liquidity opportunities, and our full-service advice.'

On the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said the exclusive Carta partnership means Carta 'will refer those private... stock plans or different corporate companies to Morgan Stanley as they move into going public,' with a commitment to make the transition 'a seamless experience for those clients.'

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya described the Carta relationship as 'a referral-based model': 'as companies began to move from a private side to a public side, they would be referred to Morgan Stanley,' and she said 'we have seen conversions into our space from the public side already over the course of this year.'

On the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026), CFO Sharon Yeshaya described the Workplace 'funnel concept': 'the first is we retain those assets' as unvested assets vest, 'and then over time... we are seeing channel migration, and that's with technology and investment, where those Workplace assets are now actually seeking advice.'

On the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya defined 'channel migration' as 'Workplace assets that began at some point in Workplace, and we're seeing them move into the advisor-led concept.'

On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), CEO Ted Pick described 'attachment points' that 'bring clients to E*TRADE' where Morgan Stanley is 'close with them in the corporate stock plan context, i.e., workplace,' and 'then ultimately, where it's appropriate, fee-based flows that make their way to the advisers.'

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said 'assets that originated from workplace continue to migrate into our advisor-led channel as a result of the consistent investments we have made into our differentiated platform.'
On the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said 'since 2020, we've seen $300 billion coming and initiating at some point from Workplace and moving into that advisor-led channel.'

On the 1Q25 earnings call (April 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said assets migrating to the advisor-led channel that originated from workplace added 'an incremental $20 billion this quarter, adding to the roughly $300 billion accumulated from workplace since we expanded our channel in 2020.'

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), management said advisor-led assets originating from workplace and E*TRADE relationships 'accelerated, growing to a record $99 billion for the full year, compared to historical averages of around $60 billion per year.'
On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), CEO Ted Pick said 'in 2025, we saw accelerating flows across channels with $100 billion migrating to financial advisors.'
The January 2026 strategic update deck shows 'Advisor-Led Flows from Workplace and E*TRADE' of ~$60 billion averaged over 2020–2024 and ~$100 billion in 2025.

On the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said 'since 2020, we have generated over $400 billion of new adviser-led assets from relationships that originated from either Workplace or E*TRADE,' that 'the total value of adviser-led assets sourced from Workplace and E*TRADE exceeds $1.2 trillion,' representing 'roughly 20% of our current $5.8 trillion of adviser-led assets.'
On the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said Morgan Stanley 'saw greater asset retention from Workplace, which translated into NNA' during the quarter as unvested assets vested.

On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said net new assets were 'a record of $148 billion' and that 'stock plan IPO flows represented just over half of the overall NNA this quarter.'
On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said Morgan Stanley has 'about 70% of the top 100 unicorns by market cap in terms of our workplace pipeline.'

On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said net new assets of $232 billion 'reflect the strength of our core business and the differentiated growth opportunities created by Workplace and the integrated firm,' and that 'IPO-related flows once again contributed to just over half of the overall NNA.'
The 2025 10-K reports workplace channel metrics of $534 billion in workplace unvested assets (2025) versus $475 billion (2024), and 6.5 million participants (2025) versus 6.6 million (2024).

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), CEO Ted Pick said the firm is 'using our scale to invest in broadening capabilities for FAs that are difficult for others to replicate: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.'

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said the firm continues to invest to deepen 'competitive moats,' citing 'our expanded collaboration with Carta in private markets and in digital assets through announced partnerships with Zero Hash.'

On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), CEO Ted Pick framed the strategy around acquisitions that fill the funnel, including acquiring 'Solium before people understand that that is the linchpin to workplace' and adding 'E*TRADE as filling out the funnel.'

On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), CFO Sharon Yeshaya attributed results to 'our sustained investments in our client acquisition funnel,' which 'allowed us to reach more clients and deepen existing relationships.'

On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), CEO Ted Pick said 'growth led by workplace relationships reflects a cornerstone of our client acquisition funnel,' and that Morgan Stanley's 'ability to serve clients across the private to public continuum continues to attract assets to our world-class platform.'

The January 2026 strategic update deck frames the approach as the Integrated Firm delivering 'unmatched capabilities throughout clients growth cycles,' spanning early-stage 'Financial Wellness and Employee Benefits' and 'Founders Wealth Strategies' through public-company 'Full-Service Wealth Advice and Asset Allocation,' 'Family Office Solutions, Trust & Estate Planning,' and 'IPO Execution and Support Services.'

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley does not break out a separate retirement-plan-only conversion metric. Its reported 'Advisor-Led Flows from Workplace and E*TRADE' combines workplace origination (which includes stock plan, retirement, and financial wellness participants) with self-directed E*TRADE origination, so retirement-specific conversion cannot be isolated from the evidence provided.
gaps.suggested_source: Workplace channel supplemental disclosure or investor materials that split advisor-led flows by origination type (stock plan vs. retirement/financial wellness vs. self-directed).

claims.text: Raymond James's 2025 Investor Day deck (published 2025-06-05) lays out the AdvisorChoice spectrum as Employee, Independent Contractor, and RIA & Custody Services, listing Employee Advisor (RJA), Advisor Select, Independent Advisor (ICD), Banks and Credit Unions, IAR (Corporate RIA), and RIA & Custody Services.

The 2025 10-K (period 2025-09-30) states Raymond James offers multiple affiliation options, which it refers to as AdvisorChoice®, and that financial advisors primarily affiliate with the firm directly as employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors ("RIAs") and broker-dealers to which it provides services through its RIA and Custody Services ("RCS") division.

The 2025 10-K describes employee financial advisors as working in a traditional branch supported by local management and administrative staff, serving predominantly retail clients, with compensation that primarily includes a payout on revenues they generate and participation in the firm's employee benefit plans.

The 2025 10-K states the independent contractor financial advisor options are designed to help advisors build their businesses with as much or as little of Raymond James's support as they determine they need, and that independent contractor financial advisors may affiliate directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in the Financial Institutions Division.

On the fiscal Q1 2026 earnings call (January 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said Raymond James has "the largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody," with "critical mass and decades of experience in all of them," and that the model is "not a new venture" or something being "tested out."

Raymond James's affiliation-options recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) describes AdvisorChoice® as the ability to match professional goals to the right affiliation option, "each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility," and describes Traditional Employee (book ownership), Advisor Select (lead your own branch with administrative support and full corporate benefits), Independent Contractor (an independent financial advisor backed by the resources of a national leader), Bank & Credit Union (national strength and local impact), and Corporate RIA (true autonomy and support refined for fee-only practices under our established RIA).
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Raymond James's affiliation-options recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) describes RIA & Custody Services as taking "strategic, financial and administrative control of your practice with a full-service partner at the ready."

claims.text: Raymond James's Advisor Select recruiting page (page content as of 2026-03-11) describes Advisor Select® as providing established advisors "the full benefits of our employee channel with the independence to create their own branches," letting them choose a location, build out an office and run the branch's P&L to earn a higher rate on production.

claims.text: On the fiscal Q3 2026 earnings call (July 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry explained there are "big differences" in how advisers spend their time day-to-day across the affiliation options: some want to dedicate close to 100% of their time to building their books and serving clients (more aligned with the employee affiliation option), while others also want to run a business—building a team, paying for benefits, and dealing with real estate, utilities and legal aspects.

Raymond James's affiliation-options recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) lists payout terms by model: Traditional Employee "Up to 50% payout" plus a "full array of competitive employee benefits"; Advisor Select "70-80% gross payout" plus a full array of competitive employee benefits; Independent Contractor "81% to 90% payout" with third-party partnerships to create a benefits package; Corporate RIA "81% to 90% payout" with third-party partnerships for benefits; Bank & Credit Union "a competitive compensation package from the financial institution in partnership with Raymond James"; and RIA & Custody Services "Work with your RIA or broker/dealer to determine compensation" and create your own benefits package.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: The same affiliation-options recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) lists qualifications by model: Traditional Employee minimum 5 years of experience with production qualifications that vary; Advisor Select minimum 3 years of experience and $3.5 million or higher in annual branch fees and commission revenue; Independent Contractor minimum 3 years of experience with a minimum T12 of $150,000 to join an existing branch and $400,000 to open a new branch; Bank & Credit Union minimum 3 years of experience and $250,000 in production; Corporate RIA minimum 3 years of experience and $50 million in assets under advisement; and RIA & Custody Services $100 million or more in assets to establish a new RIA, a minimum of $30 million to plug into an existing RIA, and $1 billion or more in AUM for introducing broker/dealers.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: The 2025 10-K states independent contractor financial advisors are "generally responsible for all of their direct costs and, accordingly, receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors."

On the fiscal Q2 2026 earnings call (April 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry explained that independent adviser payouts are higher than employee payouts "because they cover their overhead costs, their real estate, their health insurance," and that "even on the employee side, we have tiered payout systems," so as production increases an advisor moves higher up the payout grid.

On the fiscal Q3 2026 earnings call (July 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry cited a 97% adviser satisfaction rate and said Raymond James has "the largest addressable market in the industry because we have all the affiliation options that an adviser could possibly want," describing the firm as "agnostic" about how advisers affiliate and saying "we want you to fall in love with our culture, values and the platform and capabilities"; he called that combination "increasingly unique in the industry."

On the fiscal Q3 2026 earnings call (July 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said the recruiting strength "reflects our differentiated value proposition, advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities," offering "an adviser and client-focused culture along with the leading technology, products and solutions advisers need to serve clients at a high level."

On the fiscal Q3 2026 earnings call (July 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said "we don't lead with the highest check," that Raymond James wants "competitive economics" but leads with "culture and capabilities," and that "in the absence of a true differentiated value proposition, the highest check is all you have."

On the fiscal Q2 2026 earnings call (April 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said the value proposition is "becoming increasingly differentiated" because advisers "do not have to choose between culture and capabilities," and that this, combined with the "strong balance sheet, long-term thinking and commitment to independence," continues to set Raymond James apart for advisers evaluating alternatives.

On the fiscal Q2 2026 earnings call (April 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said Raymond James prefers to recruit advisers "1 by 1 versus doing acquisitions" because "100% of the transition assistance is going to retention of the adviser" and the firm can ensure recruits are "really good cultural fits for the firm."

On the fiscal Q1 2026 earnings call (January 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said recruiting is "a marathon, not a sprint" and that Raymond James wants advisors who want to be at the firm "over the long term," not "the advisors that are moving... for the highest check."

On the fiscal Q4 2025 earnings call (October 2025), CEO Paul Shoukry said the "best-of-both-worlds value proposition"—a "unique combination of an advisor and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions"—continues to resonate with advisors across all affiliation options, and that the "strong balance sheet and commitment to independence is proving to be a differentiator."

On the fiscal Q3 2025 earnings call (July 2025), CEO Paul Shoukry similarly described the "best of both worlds value proposition" and said the strong balance sheet and commitment to independence is "increasingly becoming a differentiator."

Raymond James's 2025 Investor Day deck (published 2025-06-05) frames the offering as "Multiple Affiliation Options," "Best of Both Worlds," "Advisor and Book Ownership," and "RJF Stability," to "Inspire and empower the world's best financial professionals."

The 2025 10-K states Raymond James seeks to mitigate the risk of financial advisors departing to independent RIAs "through financial advisor succession planning and by providing our financial advisors with a broad range of services and resources to support their practices."

The 2025 10-K notes that within the financial services industry other firms are offering guaranteed contracts, upfront payments, and increased compensation, and that Raymond James's financial results may be adversely affected by the costs of loans or other incentives it may offer to newly recruited financial advisors.

Raymond James's 2025 Investor Day deck (published 2025-06-05) shows domestic PCG assets under administration across its multiple affiliation models: Employee $332 billion at March 31, 2020 to $631 billion at March 31, 2025; Independent contractor $318 billion to $543 billion; RIA & Custody Services (RCS) $46 billion to $186 billion; and total domestic PCG AUA $696 billion to $1,360 billion, with 5-year CAGRs listed as 32%, 11%, 14%, and 14%.

The 2025 10-K reports total Private Client Group client assets under administration of $1.67 trillion as of September 30, 2025, of which $1.01 trillion related to fee-based accounts, and 8,943 employee and independent contractor financial advisors affiliated with Raymond James.

The 2025 10-K states financial advisors associated with firms in RCS are not included in Raymond James's financial advisor counts, although their client assets are included in AUA, and that AUA associated with RCS firms totaled $217.3 billion as of September 30, 2025.
The 2025 10-K shows Private Client Group segment net revenues of $10.18 billion for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025.
Raymond James's 2025 Investor Day deck (published 2025-06-05) shows total financial advisors of 8,011 (FY 2019), 8,787 (FY 2024), and 8,731 (March 31, 2025), a 2% 5-year CAGR.

Raymond James's fiscal Q3 2026 10-Q (period 2026-06-30) reports RCS client assets of $251.3 billion as of June 30, 2026, $228.2 billion as of March 31, 2026, and $201.6 billion as of June 30, 2025, of which $220.1 billion, $199.1 billion, and $173.9 billion were assets in fee-based accounts, respectively; revenues related to these assets are included in "Account and service fees."

The fiscal Q3 2026 10-Q states the growth in RCS client assets is partially due to transfers into RCS from Raymond James's other financial advisor channels, and that the firm would not expect these financial advisor transfers to significantly impact results of operations.

Raymond James's Bank and Credit Union Advisors recruiting page (page content as of 2026-05-17) lists 940 advisors across 160 financial institutions, $166 million in average assets under management per advisor, and $950k average advisor production.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-05-17 [IR]

claims.text: On the fiscal Q4 2025 earnings call (October 2025), CEO Paul Shoukry reported record fiscal 2025 recruiting of financial advisors to the domestic independent contractor and employee channels with trailing 12-month production at their previous firms totaling $407 million (up 21% over last year's record) and approximately $58 billion of client assets; including assets recruited into the RIA and Custody Services division, total recruited client assets over the past 12 months were nearly $63 billion.

On the fiscal Q1 2026 earnings call (January 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry reported recruiting financial advisors to the domestic independent contractor and employee channels with trailing twelve-month production totaling $96 million and approximately $13 billion of client assets for the quarter, and over the past twelve months nearly $460 million of production and over $63 billion of client assets (more than $69 billion including RCS).

On the fiscal Q2 2026 earnings call (April 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry reported recruiting financial advisers to the domestic independent contractor and employee channels with trailing 12-month production totaling $141 million and nearly $21 billion of client assets at their previous firms—the second highest quarterly result in the firm's history in terms of both recruited production and assets.

On the fiscal Q3 2026 earnings call (July 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry reported recruiting financial advisers to the domestic independent contractor and employee channels with trailing 12-month production totaling $156 million and nearly $23 billion of client assets at their previous firms during the quarter.

On the fiscal Q3 2026 earnings call (July 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said that through the first 9 months of fiscal 2026 Raymond James recruited advisers with trailing 12-month production totaling $393 million and more than $56 billion of client assets at their previous firms.

Raymond James's fiscal Q3 2026 supplement reports domestic Private Client Group net new assets of $21,692 million (5.5% annualized) for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 and $75,474 million (6.6% annualized) for the nine months ended June 30, 2026; its fiscal Q2 2026 supplement reports $22,954 million (5.8% annualized) for the quarter ended March 31, 2026; and its fiscal Q1 2026 supplement reports $30,828 million (8.0% annualized) for the quarter ended December 31, 2025.
claims.source_label: RJF supplement 2026-06-30, p.5 [IR]; RJF supplement 2026-03-31, p.5 [IR]; RJF supplement 2025-12-31, p.5 [IR]

claims.text: The fiscal Q3 2026 press release (period 2026-06-30) reports record Private Client Group assets under administration of $1.86 trillion and record quarter-end PCG assets in fee-based accounts of $1.15 trillion as of June 30, 2026, with PCG quarterly pre-tax income of $423 million and quarterly PCG net revenues that rose 14% year-over-year.
