claims.text: The 2025 10-K states Schwab's largest sources of net revenues are net interest revenue, asset management and administration fees, trading revenue, and bank deposit account fees, supported by its broker-dealer, bank, and asset management subsidiaries.

The 2025 10-K states net interest revenue is the difference between interest generated on interest-earning assets and interest paid on funding sources; Schwab's primary funding source for interest-earning assets is uninvested client cash balances held on its balance sheet, and interest-earning assets are primarily high-quality fixed income securities, margin loans, and bank loans.

The 2025 10-K states asset management and administration fees are primarily earned from proprietary money market mutual funds, proprietary and third-party mutual funds and ETFs, and fee-based managed investing solutions.

The 2025 10-K states trading revenue includes commissions for executing client trades in certain individual equities, options, futures, fixed income securities, and certain third-party mutual funds and ETFs; order flow revenue; and principal transactions revenue earned primarily from actions to support client trading in fixed income securities.

The 2025 10-K reports 2024 total net revenues of $19.6 billion (up 4%): net interest revenue of $9.1 billion (down 3%), asset management and administration fees of $5.7 billion (up 20%), trading revenue of $3.3 billion (up 1%), and bank deposit account fee revenue of $729 million (up 3%).

The 2025 10-K reports 2025 total net revenues of $23.9 billion (up 22%): net interest revenue of $11.8 billion (up 28%), asset management and administration fees of $6.5 billion (up 14%), trading revenue of $3.9 billion (up 20%), and bank deposit account fee revenue of $977 million (up 34%).

The 2025 10-K states client cash balances are a significant funding source for revenue: cash awaiting investment may be used to extend margin loans to clients or be swept to banking subsidiaries to fund loans and investment securities, and a portion is swept to the TD Depository Institutions under the 2023 IDA agreement, through which Schwab earns bank deposit account fees.

The 2Q26 press release (July 2026) reports net interest margin of 3.00%, client transactional sweep cash of $485.7 billion at quarter-end, average interest-earning assets of $445.0 billion (up 5% vs 2Q25), asset management and administration fees of $1.8 billion (up 16%), and trading revenue of $1.2 billion (up 28%).

The 3Q26 press release (October 2026) reports net interest margin of 3.04%, client transactional sweep cash of $492.8 billion (up $7.1 billion vs the prior quarter-end), average interest-earning assets of $451.5 billion (up 8% vs 3Q25), asset management and administration fees of $1.9 billion (up 14%), and trading revenue of $1.2 billion (up 16%).

The 2Q26 investor deck (July 2026) lists Schwab's annualized revenue sensitivities: net interest revenue +/- 25 bps in the target Fed Funds rate of roughly $250M-$300M; AMAF +/- 1% in the S&P 500 of roughly $35M; client trading +/- 100K DATs of roughly $40M; margin balances +/- $1B of roughly $20M; and bank sweep balances +/- $1B of roughly $35M.

The 2025 10-K states that within Morgan Stanley's Wealth Management segment, asset management revenues are related to advisory services associated with fee-based assets, account service and administration, and distribution of products, and are generally based on the net asset value of the account in which a client is invested.

On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said Wealth Management asset management revenues were $5.3 billion and transactional revenues were $1.2 billion (up 20% year-over-year); deposits grew to $436 billion and net interest income increased to $2.3 billion, which she said outperformed on higher-than-expected sweep balances and strong loan growth.

The 3Q26 press release reports Morgan Stanley Wealth Management record net revenues of $9.1 billion and record pre-tax income of $2.8 billion (30.4% pre-tax margin), with net revenues up 10% driven by record asset management revenues on asset growth, transactional revenues on client engagement, and net interest income on lending growth and higher average sweep deposits.

The 2025 10-K states Edward Jones broadly categorizes net revenues into fee revenue (asset-based fees plus account and activity fees), trade revenue (commissions and principal transactions), net interest and dividends revenue, and other revenue; asset-based fees include advisory program fees based on the average daily market value of client assets and contractual rates.

The 2025 10-K states Edward Jones' trade revenue is composed of commissions earned from the distribution of mutual fund shares and insurance products and the purchase or sale of securities, plus principal transactions revenue primarily from distribution and participation in principal trading in municipal obligations, certificates of deposit and corporate obligations.

The 2025 10-K states Edward Jones earns service fees and revenue sharing from mutual fund and insurance companies, cash solutions revenue from the Edward Jones Insured Bank Deposit Program, asset-based fees from trust services through Edward Jones Trust Company, and investment management fees as adviser to the Edward Jones Money Market Fund.

The 2Q26 10-Q (six months ended June 26, 2026) disaggregates Edward Jones revenue: total asset-based fee revenue of $7,993 million (advisory programs fees $6,396 million, service fees $890 million, cash solutions fees $263 million, other asset-based fees $444 million), total trade revenue of $910 million (commissions $799 million, principal transactions $111 million), and net interest and dividends and other revenue of $401 million, within net revenue of $9,679 million.

The 2Q26 10-Q reports Edward Jones ended 2Q26 with $2.6 trillion of assets under care, including $1.2 trillion of advisory programs AUC; net revenue increased 18% to $5,002 primarily on higher asset-based fee revenue, partially offset by lower interest and dividends revenue due to a lower interest rate environment.

The 2025 10-K reports Merrill Wealth Management revenue of $20.7 billion increased nine percent, primarily driven by higher asset management fees (reflecting higher market valuations and positive AUM flows) and higher brokerage fees from increased transactional volume.

The 2Q26 10-Q reports GWIM net interest income of $1.9 billion (up $126 million, driven by loan and deposit growth) and noninterest income of $5.0 billion, including asset management fees up 19% to $4.4 billion and higher brokerage fees from increased transactional volume.

On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), CFO Alastair Borthwick said GWIM is 'primarily a fee-based advice-driven model,' with about 30% of revenue in net interest income derived from GWIM clients and the large loan and deposit balances.

The 2025 10-K states Raymond James' PCG segment provides financial planning, investment advisory, and securities transaction services for which it generally charges either asset-based fees (in 'Asset management and related administrative fees') or sales commissions (in 'Brokerage revenues'), and earns distribution and related service revenues for mutual funds, annuities, and insurance products.

The 2025 10-K states Raymond James earns RJBDP servicing fees from banks for administrative services on clients' swept deposits; third-party bank fees are variable and fluctuate with client cash balances and the level of short-term interest rates relative to interest paid to clients, and PCG also earns fees from Raymond James' Bank segment.

The 2025 10-K states Raymond James' PCG segment also includes net interest earnings primarily on assets segregated for regulatory purposes, margin loans, cash balances, and securities borrowing transactions, net of interest paid on client cash balances in the Client Interest Program and securities lending transactions.

The 2Q26 10-Q (quarter ended June 30, 2026) reports Raymond James asset management and related administrative fees increased $272 million (19%) on higher assets in fee-based accounts; brokerage revenues increased $65 million (15%) on higher client activity and trailing revenues; and account and service fees increased $9 million (2%), with RJBDP fees from third-party banks declining as average balances swept to third-party banks declined.

On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), Schwab CEO Rick Wurster said clients in Schwab Wealth Advisory generate 3x the ROCA (revenue on client assets) of Schwab's retail clients, that just 5% of Schwab retail households are in a fee-based advice solution, and that 31% of Schwab clients said they are willing to pay for advice.
On the same 2Q26 call, Schwab CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab's self-directed investor base creates an 'unmatched conversion funnel into advice' that will 'diversify our economics over the long term.'

The 2025 10-K describes Schwab's self-directed offering (digital and software-based trading platforms, research tools, and multichannel support) alongside its advisory solutions, including Schwab Wealth Advisory's dedicated Wealth Advisor and referrals to independent RIAs through Schwab Advisor Network, with advisory minimum investments starting at $5,000.

The 2025 10-K states Schwab's largest revenue sources are net interest revenue (funded primarily by uninvested client cash), asset management and administration fees, trading revenue, and bank deposit account fees.
The 2025 10-K states Edward Jones' composition of net revenue is heavily weighted towards asset-based fee revenue, which is earned on the market value of the underlying client assets.

On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), Bank of America CFO Alastair Borthwick said GWIM is primarily a fee-based, advice-driven model, with about 30% of revenue in net interest income from client loan and deposit balances.
The 2025 10-K states Morgan Stanley's Wealth Management asset management revenues are generally based on the net asset value of the fee-based account in which a client is invested.

On the March 2026 quarter earnings call (April 2026), Raymond James CEO Paul Shoukry said industry cash transactional/sweep balances have declined 40% to 50% and fee-based accounts now hold less than $10,000 in average cash per account; he contrasted advisor-led models, where a financial advisor helps clients reinvest cash, with e-brokers where no financial advisor is involved.

Fitch, as reported by trade press (September 2026), identified Schwab as having the largest absolute earnings exposure to client cash, reflecting its substantially larger sweep-related deposit base, and noted Schwab generated nearly $3.4 billion in net interest revenue in Q2 2026, largely on approximately $485.7 billion held in sweep accounts.

The 2Q26 10-Q reports Schwab's net interest margin was 3.00% in 2Q26 and 2.94% in the first six months of 2026 (versus 2.66% and 2.59% in the prior-year periods), and presents asset management and administration fees together with average client assets and average fee yields.
The 1Q26 10-Q reports Schwab's net interest margin was 2.88% in 1Q26 (versus 2.53% in 1Q25), and presents asset management and administration fees with average client assets and average fee yields.
The 3Q26 press release reports Schwab's net interest margin expanded to 3.04%.
The 2025 10-K states Schwab's management uses 'total expenses excluding interest as a percentage of average client assets' as a measure of operating efficiency.
On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), Schwab CEO Rick Wurster used ROCA ('revenue on client assets') as the metric, saying Schwab Wealth Advisory clients generate 3x the ROCA of retail clients.

The 2Q26 10-Q states Edward Jones' client margin loans averaged $4.2 billion and earned interest at an average annual rate of approximately 636 basis points (6.36%), and investments averaged $16.6 billion and earned approximately 370 basis points (3.70%), during the first six months of 2026.

The 2025 10-K states Edward Jones' client margin loans averaged $3.6 billion and earned approximately 707 basis points (7.07%), and investments averaged $17.0 billion and earned approximately 420 basis points (4.20%), in 2025.
The 1Q26 10-Q reports Raymond James net interest margin (net yield on interest-earning assets) of 2.81% for the Bank segment and 2.74% firmwide, versus 2.67% and 2.77% a year earlier.
On the March 2026 quarter earnings call (April 2026), CFO Jonathan Oorlog said the average yield on Raymond James RJBDP balances with third-party banks decreased 6 basis points to 2.7%.

claims.text: Digital-first, virtual delivery will keep expanding — A 2025 advisor-search study (published August 2025) anticipates continued growth in AI tool usage for advisor searches, increasing expectation for faster response times and digital-first communications, and further acceptance of virtual advisor relationships regardless of geographic location.

Digital platforms and multichannel support anchor self-directed advice — Schwab's 2025 10-K states that self-directed clients receive 'robust digital and software based trading platforms, real-time market data, research tools, and multichannel support,' with Schwab Trading Powered by Ameritrade® offering the thinkorswim® suite, specialized education and 24/7 support.

Digital-first expansion is a named initiative — Edward Jones's 2025 10-K describes its initiatives as including 'a new digital platform, focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors,' alongside High Net Worth and Workplace initiatives.

Digital adoption in GWIM is already high — Bank of America's 3Q26 GWIM materials show 85% of relationships receiving statements electronically and 69% of check deposits made through digital channels, and its 3Q26 GWIM highlights report 56% of eligible investment, trust and banking accounts opened through digital onboarding.
claims.source_label: BAC deck 2026-09-30, p.22 [IR]; BAC press - GWIM segment 2026-09-30 [filing]

claims.text: Digital estate planning and around-the-clock trading expand delivery — Schwab's CEO said on the 1Q25 earnings call (April 2025) that Schwab made a strategic investment in wealth.com, 'a leader in digital estate planning,' and expanded its trader offer with '24x5 trading capability on our Thinkorswim platform.'

Digital delivery brings rising technology and cyber risk — Bank of America's 2025 10-K states that acceptance of digital banking, mobile products and remote access tools 'have resulted in increased reliance on virtual or digital interactions,' increasing cybersecurity, breach and technology-failure risk.

Firms are expected to supervise digital channels — FINRA's 2025 effective practices (published December 2025) describe supervisory procedures for mobile apps and reasonably designed procedures for digital communication channels, including monitoring new tools/features, training, and video content protocols.

Personal-finance apps are being pulled into advisor workflows — The trade press reported in August 2026 that Edward Jones took a minority stake in Quicken as a step toward integrating its personal financial management capabilities to support advisor conversations, while noting Edward Jones is still determining the deployment strategy.

AI is expected to be broadly transformative — Accenture's 2025 research reports 97% say AI will have a transformative effect on the future of financial advice to a moderate or great extent in the next three years.

AI will accelerate firms' strategies and open new channels — Schwab's CEO said on the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026) that 'Schwab is already an AI-enabled company,' that AI will accelerate its strategy, and that 'AI opens up new distribution channels and allows us to create personalized relationships with clients we have not been able to serve with a person-to-person relationship.'

AI will be used mostly for administrative and next-best-action work — Accenture's 2025 research reports 55% say AI will be most helpful in eliminating administrative tasks, identifying next best action opportunities, and automating marketing and client contact activities.

Agentic AI will handle preparation, monitoring and routine servicing — Deloitte's 2026 research says Morgan Stanley's AI Debrief automatically summarizes meetings, generates follow-ups and logs notes into the customer relationship management system, and describes an 'AI-native' stage where advisers 'operate with a team of digital agents, supervising AI systems that handle preparation, monitoring, and routine servicing.'

GenAI will enable 24/7 client service and compliance support — McKinsey's 2025 research says chatbots and virtual assistants save advisors time on knowledge management and enable advisors to provide 24/7 client service, while genAI can streamline risk and compliance processes and enhance fraud monitoring.

AI will prepare advisors for personalized planning — Bank of America's CEO said on the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025) that in wealth management AI helps relationship managers and advisors search and summarize information, preparing them to deliver personalized planning and personalized pitches to clients, with copilots helping organize the prospecting process.

Firm data and scale will help tailor advice — Morgan Stanley's CEO said on the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026) that with '$8.4 trillion of assets in wealth management' and getting to 21 million households, the firm's data insights 'allow our FAs to tailor advice and equip our own tools to deliver that advice.'

Robo-advice and fintech will intensify competition — Edward Jones's 2025 10-K states the industry is evolving with 'artificial intelligence technologies and lower cost, computer-based "robo-advice,"' and that it faces competition from robo-advisors, lower-cost options, and 'fintech' companies with internet- and mobile-based platforms.

A minority expects AI to eventually compete for clients — Accenture's 2025 research reports 40% believe AI can achieve a level of sophisticated advice and planning that will ultimately leave advisors competing with an algorithm for clients in the next 12 months.

AI output carries accuracy, bias and security risk — Raymond James's 2025 10-K states AI development could produce 'inaccurate output' or rely on 'biased, incomplete, and/or inaccurate datasets,' and poses security and privacy risks it mitigates with 'walled-garden' environments.

Generative AI summaries are disclosed as potentially inaccurate — Schwab's 2Q26 press release describes its generative AI 'Portfolio Insights' feature and discloses that it 'should not be construed as investment advice or recommendations' and that 'generative AI output may be inaccurate, containing hallucinated, stale, or incomplete information.'

Automation is being paired with professional oversight — Merrill's September 2026 press release describes Tax Efficient Transition and Dollar Cost Averaging services that 'combine automation with professional portfolio oversight' to help clients simplify asset transitions and cash deployment within personalized investment strategies.

AI replaces tasks, not the advisor's human role — McKinsey's 2026 research concludes AI will quickly replace tasks such as preparation, extraction, drafting and scenario planning, but 'replacing tasks is not the same as replacing the advisor's role as the human accountable for judgment, trust, and behavioral coaching.'

Human advice carries more emotional value than digital — Vanguard's 2025 research reports 88% of human-advice clients reported more peace of mind compared with managing their own finances, while 69% of digital advice clients experienced significant increases in peace of mind, and notes human advice value is mostly derived from the client's relationship with the advisor.

Emotional reassurance is beyond robo-advisors — The 2025 advisor-search study reports 28% named 'helping me feel less financial stress and anxiety' as the most valuable advisor role, 'highlighting emotional factors that investing apps and robo-advisors can't provide.'

Trusted relationships cannot be replicated by technology — Raymond James's CEO said on the earnings call for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 that what sets the firm apart is 'the way our financial professionals and advisers serve clients through trusted relationships. That can't be replicated by AI or technology, but it will be helped by AI and technology.'

Advisors will orchestrate specialists through augmented intelligence — Capgemini's 2026 World Wealth Report describes advisory roles redefined so relationship managers 'leverage augmented intelligence to orchestrate experiences across the full wealth ecosystem,' coordinating specialists in tax, estate planning, lending and philanthropy, and positions lead relationship managers as 'experience orchestrators' under 'trusted human-AI collaboration.'

Humans are brought in when judgment is needed — Deloitte's 2026 research says agentic AI orchestration can track deadlines, needs and opportunities continuously, 'while bringing in the human adviser when judgment or a client conversation is needed,' and may shift the model toward teaming, specialization and technology leverage.

Advisor-led advice is still drawing assets — Morgan Stanley's CEO said on the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026) that in 2025 '$100 billion' migrated to financial advisors, and the firm is investing in broadening FA capabilities in alternatives/privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office/OCIO, and tailored lending.

AI tools expand advisors' capacity to deliver advice at scale — Bank of America's CFO said on the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026) that 'Advisor productivity, disciplined pricing, digital engagement and AI tools continue to expand our capacity to deliver personalized advice at scale.'

AI should free advisors for deeper relationships, not replace them — Raymond James's CEO said on the earnings call for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 that he would not trust certain family financial situations 'to an AI bot no matter how good the algorithm is,' and that AI should help advisers produce more bespoke tailored insights, save time on administrative tasks, and allow more time for deeply personal relationships.

Client experience will shift from episodic to continuous, context-aware journeys — Capgemini's 2026 research describes an 'Adaptive Experience AI Engine,' a 'Unified Client Semantics Profile,' and a 'Personal Wealth Coach' that enable 'a shift from episodic interactions to continuous, context-aware wealth and retirement experiences.'

Experience will be differentiated across the wealth continuum — Bank of America's 2025 investor day deck positions its wealth businesses to serve mass market clients with a 'predominantly digital experience,' mass affluent clients with 'goals-based advice' and 'guidance delivered at scale,' high net worth clients with 'dedicated advice' and 'solutions for complex needs,' and ultra high net worth clients with a 'sophisticated approach' to 'managing generational wealth.'

Clients will have choice across channels — Morgan Stanley's 2025 10-K states its Wealth Management competes across 'advisor led, workplace and digital direct' channels, with technology supporting 'evolving client needs, including generative artificial intelligence and tokenization.'

Firms are positioning around 'AI + Human Expertise' — Schwab's 2026 investor day deck lists 'AI + Human Expertise' among the elements it says position Schwab to 'delight clients & drive diversified revenue growth,' alongside 'Trusted Brand,' 'Exceptional Value' and 'One-Stop Shop.'

Advice saves clients time and provides emotional benefits — Vanguard's 2025 research reports clients' time savings come from portfolio monitoring (61%), investment selection (60%), trust in the advisor (54%), and peace of mind (50%).

Next-generation clients want transparency and broader life guidance — Fidelity's 2025 Investor Insights Study says wealthy next-generation households 'seek transparency in advisor compensation, broader life guidance beyond investment management, and emerging investment products such as active ETFs, liquid alternatives, and cryptocurrencies.'

Transparency and personalization remain key client expectations — The 2025 advisor-search study lists top hesitations as pushy/aggressive sales tactics (53.0%), lack of transparency about fees or commissions (38.4%), and one-size-fits-all advice (20.2%).

Technology is expected to free advisors for face-to-face client time — Raymond James's 2025 Voice of the Advisor survey quotes advisors saying firm technology 'will help create capacity and free more time to spend face-to-face with clients' and lets them 'spend less time managing my office and more time connecting with clients.'

New products will broaden the client experience — Schwab's 2Q26 10-Q describes a phased rollout of Schwab Crypto™ giving retail clients direct access to bitcoin and ether trading combined with educational content, with plans to add more cryptocurrencies and in-kind deposit and withdrawal transfer capabilities.

Automated services aim to keep clients focused on long-term goals — Merrill's September 2026 press release quotes its Head of Fiduciary Programs and Platforms saying the new Tax Efficient Transition and Dollar Cost Averaging services 'help clients to stay focused on their long-term financial goals.'

claims.text: p1 - Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (period 2025-12-31, published 2026-03-13) states the financial services industry continues to evolve technologically, 'including the utilization of artificial intelligence technologies and lower cost, computer-based "robo-advice",' and that Edward Jones faces risk from these accelerated changes and competitive forces.
p1 - Edward Jones: In the same 2025 10-K, Edward Jones lists as an aspiration to 'Be a knowledge-powered advice firm by delivering leading data-powered insights to better serve clients.'

p1 - Edward Jones: WealthManagement.com trade press (published 2026-09-30) reported Edward Jones has partnered with Aboon, an AI-driven third-party administrator, and Retirement Plan Advisory Group to develop an end-to-end retirement plan management tool; principal Katherine Roy said the firm wants to 'create those opportunities for advisors' to serve business owners and expand access to retirement plans.

p1 - Charles Schwab: On the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026), CEO Rick Wurster said 'Schwab is already an AI-enabled company,' that Schwab has used machine learning and AI capabilities for years, and that AI will accelerate Schwab's strategy.

p1 - Charles Schwab: Schwab's 2Q26 press release (July 2026) describes Portfolio Insights as a generative AI feature that provides a narrative snapshot of a client portfolio's day change, recaps news on top S&P 500 movers, and surfaces Schwab expert content—with a disclosure that it is for informational and educational purposes only and 'should not be construed as investment advice or recommendations.'

p1 - Charles Schwab: Schwab's 3Q26 press release (October 2026) announced it introduced 'Charley, a new AI-powered assistant' for U.S. retail clients and 'partnered with Anthropic to bring Claude for Financial Advisors directly to the independent RIAs Schwab serves.'

p1 - Bank of America (company-wide): On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), CEO Brian Moynihan said artificial intelligence and machine learning allow Bank of America 'to change the work across many more areas of our company' than prior tools, noting headcount fell from 300,000 fifteen years ago to 212,000 today.
p1 - Bank of America: BofA's 2025 investor-day deck (November 2025) lists an 'AI-powered digital assistant for teammates' and '100% of Private Bank teammates with access to AI tools.'

p1 - Bank of America Private Bank: The 2026 Private Bank Study of Wealthy Americans (June 2026) states Bank of America Private Bank 'uses AI to support advisor capacity, deepen client relationships, and help teams find information faster and more efficiently.'

p1 - Bank of America GWIM: In the GWIM segment of the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), CFO Alastair Borthwick said 'new AI-enabled tools' help advisers prepare for client conversations, identify opportunities and deliver more personalized advice at scale.
p1 - Bank of America GWIM: In the GWIM segment of the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), Borthwick said 'AI tools continue to expand our capacity to deliver personalized advice at scale.'

p1 - Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said Morgan Stanley's early AI use cases include DevGen AI (developer efficiency), Parable (data analysis and summarization), and LeadIQ, an 'AI-powered lead distribution platform' matching workplace and self-directed relationships to financial advisors.

p1 - Morgan Stanley: On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), CEO Ted Pick said Morgan Stanley's growth plans 'embed the increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and inside our client base.'

p1 - Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley's 2025 10-K cites generative artificial intelligence and tokenization among the technology factors affecting its Wealth Management competition across advisor-led, workplace and digital direct channels.

p1 - Raymond James: Raymond James's 2025 10-K (November 2025) states the firm 'use[s], develop[s], and incorporate[s] within our technology platform and services, systems and tools that incorporate AI and machine learning, including generative AI,' with governance processes and proprietary or 'walled-garden' environments to protect data.

p1 - Raymond James: Raymond James's 2025 investor-day deck (June 2025) lays out an AI framework whose pillars include 'Empower Advisors: Integrate AI tools into our advisor platform that reduce the administrative workload,' plus driving operational excellence, fostering innovation, safety/responsibility, and data-driven insights.

p1 - Raymond James: On the earnings call for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (published July 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said Raymond James completed the enterprise rollout of Raimond, its proprietary AI assistant, giving people 'a secure plain language way to access institutional knowledge, ask follow-up questions and receive more actionable answers.'

p1 - Raymond James: Raymond James's 2025 investor-day deck lists advisor-facing tools including 'RJnet & Advisor Access GenAI Search,' 'Zoom AI Meeting Summaries,' 'Microsoft CoPilot' and the 'NASH Platform.'

p1 - Raymond James: Raymond James's fiscal 2Q26 press release (April 2026) states the firm continues 'increasing AI integration, to improve efficiency and provide our financial professionals with more time to serve their clients.'

p1 - Research (FINRA): FINRA's 2025 oversight report notes generative AI use cases 'are emerging quickly in the financial industry' and shares the most common GenAI use cases FINRA has observed among member firms.

p1 - Research (McKinsey): McKinsey's 2025 report describes how GenAI chatbots/virtual assistants ('AI task organizers, next best action') can save advisors time, enable 24/7 client service, and help advisors simulate scenarios and process financial data for more informed advice.
p2 - Charles Schwab: On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), CEO Rick Wurster said AI is driving efficiencies, citing that 'developer team productivity has improved by 15% to 20%' over the past year.

p2 - Charles Schwab: On the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026), Wurster cited that '77% of U.S. investors use AI today, though more than 90% still prefer human involvement in addition to AI'—an investor-level figure, not Schwab tool adoption.
p2 - Bank of America: BofA's 2025 investor-day deck reports '100% of Private Bank teammates with access to AI tools.'

p3 - Charles Schwab: Schwab's 2Q26 deck states 'AI continues to amplify our advantage, creating more personalized client experiences & greater productivity at scale.'

p4 - Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K risk factors state Edward Jones 'has engaged in significant digital initiatives to modernize its technology and expects to continue to do so in the future,' and that failing to enhance technology at industry pace could decrease client and colleague satisfaction and retention.

p4 - Charles Schwab: On the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), Wurster said Schwab's 'greatest advantage comes from combining people with AI-powered capabilities to create deeper relationships that scale with our clients' needs.'

p4 - Bank of America GWIM: In the GWIM segment of the 2Q26 earnings call (July 2026), CFO Alastair Borthwick said AI-enabled tools 'help advisers prepare for client conversations, identify opportunities and deliver more personalized advice at scale.'
p4 - Bank of America GWIM: In the GWIM segment of the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), Borthwick said 'AI tools continue to expand our capacity to deliver personalized advice at scale.'
p4 - Bank of America: BofA's 2025 investor-day deck lists 'our use of AI to drive innovation and improve productivity' among its forward-looking statements.

p4 - Morgan Stanley: On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), CEO Ted Pick said growth plans embed increasing adoption of AI tools and that confidence 'continues to increase in the potential for both the efficiency and the effectiveness of AI-related technologies across the business units and infrastructure.'

p4 - Raymond James: On the earnings call for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (published July 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said Raymond James will 'continue investing in automation, process improvement and AI as part of our more than $1.1 billion annual technology spend,' while 'keeping personal relationships at the center.'

claims.text: Shift to fee-based is a decade-long trend - Cerulli (published 2025-05-28) reports: 'For the past decade, financial firms have shifted their compensation models from largely commission-based to an asset-related fee structure,' and fee-based payments are preferred by 36% of affluent investors.

Actual compensation still spans models - the same Cerulli report (2025-05-28) finds 33% of affluent investors compensate via an asset-based fee, 21% use a no-fee platform, and 20% use a commission-based method of payment.

Recurring-revenue vs transactional models - a December 2023 research report (published 2023-12-20) found advisors whose income from clients was commission-based or hourly showed lower levels of wellbeing than those generating income in a recurring-revenue relationship model (e.g., AUM or subscription fees).

Flat and subscription pricing are emerging - an August 2025 research report (published 2025-08-13) lists common fee models as asset-based (typically 0.5% to 1.5% annually), hourly ($150-$500+ per hour), flat project fees, or monthly subscription fees.

Flat and hourly pricing disclosed - Raymond James's advisory brochure (published 2026-09-14) states planning fees can be structured as an hourly rate or fixed (flat) dollar fee, and investment consulting fees as hourly, fixed (flat) dollar, or up to an annual rate of 2.25% of assets, with hourly fees generally up to $400 per hour.
Asset-management fee levels disclosed - the 2025 Bank of America 10-K (published 2026-02-25) states asset management fees 'generally range from 50 basis points (bps) to 150 bps of the AUM.'

Fee-based funnel expansion - on the 3Q26 Morgan Stanley earnings call (October 2026), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said investments across workplace, self-directed and advisory channels 'increases the breadth of the funnel, moves it to fee-based,' and expands margins over time.
Fee-based flows scaling - on the 4Q25 Morgan Stanley earnings call (January 2026), the firm reported full-year fee-based flows of $160 billion and net new assets of $356 billion.

Advice conversion opportunity - on the 2Q26 Schwab earnings call (July 2026), CEO Rick Wurster said just 5% of Schwab retail households are in a fee-based advice solution and 31% of Schwab clients said they are willing to pay for advice.

Advisory program growth - the Edward Jones 2026 Q2 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) states advisory programs' average AUC increased 28% due to higher average market levels and 'the increased investment of client dollars into advisory programs.'

Fee-based programs described - the Edward Jones 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) describes Guided Solutions as a client-directed advisory program and Guided Portfolios as a non-discretionary, fee-based program.

Fee-based vs commission choice disclosed - Merrill's advisory brochure (published 2026-10-30) tells clients to consider 'Your preference for a fee-based or commission-based relationship' when comparing account types and advisory programs.

Fee-based suitability framing - Edward Jones's advisory brochure (published 2026-03-27) states fee-based clients should be 'comfortable paying monthly, asset-based (percentage) fees... rather than individual, transaction-based commissions or sales charges.'

Commission-to-fee transition is contested - the Edward Jones 3Q25 10-Q (published 2025-11-07) discloses a putative class action alleging the firm 'inappropriately transitioned client dollars from commission-based accounts to fee-based programs.'

Compression then stabilization - a February 2025 McKinsey report (published 2025-02-10) states that after a period of fee compression for advisory relationships from 2013 to 2018, fee rates have stabilized; $1.0 million to $1.5 million advisory relationships have stayed at an average of approximately 104 basis points since 2019.

Fee pressure expected to be uneven - an April 2026 McKinsey report (published 2026-04-08) says fee rates for relationships of more than $1 million have remained 'remarkably steady at about 104 basis points since 2019' and expects fee pressure as 'demands for transparency and unbundled pricing rather than a blanket reduction in basis points.'

Price competition compresses margins - the 2025 Raymond James 10-K (published 2025-11-25) states regulatory requirements have produced 'greater price transparency, leading to price competition and decreased trading margins,' and trading margins are further compressed by the shift from high- to low-touch services; it expects pricing pressures to continue.

AI-driven cost relief vs fee pressure - a May 2026 Deloitte report (published 2026-05-20) says lower cost-to-serve can expand margins for firms that execute and maintain pricing, while 'competitive pressure may compress fees as planning outputs become easier to compare.'

Price competition framed as value, not cheapest - an August 2025 research report (published 2025-08-13) says 48% consider pricing among top factors but 'this isn't about being cheapest, it's about demonstrating clear value for your fees.'

Firm openness to pricing evolution - on the Raymond James fiscal 2Q26 earnings call (April 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said the firm wants 'a profitable and competitive and fair pricing structure' and would be 'flexible and open to evolving' if industry pricing evolves based on competitive pressures and client preferences.
Market-linked fee pressure - the 2025 Bank of America 10-K (published 2026-02-25) states declines in AUM values 'can result in lower fees earned for managing such assets.'

Asset-based revenue concentration risk - the 2025 Edward Jones 10-K (published 2026-03-13) states net revenue is heavily weighted toward asset-based fee revenue and a decrease in the market value of assets could have a negative impact on results.

Fee waivers in low-rate environments - the 2025 Edward Jones 10-K states that in low interest rate environments the Partnership has waived certain fees to maintain a positive client yield, which could happen again.

Outlooks differ on fee pressure - an April 2026 McKinsey report predicts fee pressure as 'demands for transparency and unbundled pricing rather than a blanket reduction in basis points,' while a May 2026 Deloitte report says 'competitive pressure may compress fees as planning outputs become easier to compare'; the two research reports differ on whether pressure compresses fee levels or primarily reshapes pricing structure.

Transparency is the top trust factor - an August 2025 research report (published 2025-08-13) says nearly three-quarters (73%) of survey participants said transparency in fees and services is crucial for establishing an advisor's credibility.

Fee components are disclosed - Edward Jones's advisory brochure (published 2026-03-27) explains its Advisory Solutions Fund Models Fee 'includes a Program Fee and a Platform Fee,' and Eligible Investments have internal fees and expenses described in each fund's prospectus.
Pricing-group disclosure - the same Edward Jones brochure (2026-03-27) states 'we will disclose to you the accounts making up your Pricing Group upon request.'

Negotiated fee reductions disclosed - Edward Jones's brochure (2026-03-27) states the Advisory Solutions Fund Models Fee may be lower than the maximum annual fee rate where Edward Jones or the financial advisor negotiates a lower Program Fee, or for active or eligible retired associates and members of their Pricing Group.

Total cost comparisons - Schwab's advisory brochure (published 2026-10-15) states the SWA Program cost 'may be higher or lower than paying separately,' and certain performance reports show returns net of the SWA Fee while others show gross.

Advisory vs brokerage cost comparison - Morgan Stanley's advisory brochure (published 2026-11-04) explains advisory accounts use the lower-cost advisory share class but pay an asset-based fee, so total mutual fund costs 'may be higher or lower' than brokerage.

Lowest-cost share class practice - Merrill's advisory brochure (published 2026-10-30) states assets are generally invested in the lowest cost eligible mutual fund share class, and advisors' compensation is not affected by the share class selected.

Some charges remain not separately itemized - Merrill's brochure (2026-10-30) states foreign trading and currency conversion charges 'are included in the net price of the security' and 'will not be reflected as separate charges on your trade confirmations or account statements,' though it will obtain the amount upon written request.
Embedded fund fees are not in the statement - Morgan Stanley's brochure (2026-11-04) states fund fees and expenses 'are not included in the Fee amount in your account statements.'

Expense disaggregation standard - Raymond James's 2Q FY2026 10-Q (published 2026-08-05) states FASB ASU 2024-03 will require disaggregated expense disclosures providing 'enhanced transparency into the nature and function of expenses,' effective fiscal 2028.

Expense disclosure standard - Edward Jones's 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) states ASU 2024-03 requires disclosure of specified costs and expenses and adoption will not have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements.
Unbundling as a signpost - an April 2026 McKinsey report (published 2026-04-08) lists 'sustained unbundling' among signposts of whether a bear case is materializing.

Disclosure rules cover fees and costs - the 2025 Edward Jones 10-K (published 2026-03-13) states Edward Jones is subject to Regulation Best Interest and the SEC rule requiring Form CRS delivery with 'information on fees, costs, conflicts of interest.'

Reg BI and Form CRS implementation - the 2025 Raymond James 10-K (published 2025-11-25) states implementing Reg BI and Form CRS resulted in review and modification of policies and 'implementation of additional client disclosures,' plus advisor education and training.

Fiduciary and Reg BI standards - the 2025 Morgan Stanley 10-K (published 2026-02-19) states MSSB's advisory relationships are subject to fiduciary obligations, and Reg BI requires broker-dealers to act in the best interest of retail customers.
Regulation covers fee arrangements - the 2025 Schwab 10-K (published 2026-02-25) states securities regulation covers, among other things, 'fee arrangements... and disclosure to clients.'
Brochure as fiduciary disclosure - Merrill's advisory brochure (published 2026-10-30) states it is a fiduciary and 'This Brochure is a key element in meeting this disclosure obligation.'
Full disclosure commitment - Morgan Stanley's advisory brochure (published 2026-11-04) states it will provide 'full disclosure of all material facts' and clearly disclose the details of conflicts.

Disclosure enforcement - Merrill's brochure (2026-10-30) discloses an April 2023 SEC order finding MLPF&S failed to disclose a 'production credit' charged in addition to foreign currency mark-ups/downs, resulting in a cease-and-desist order, censure, and a penalty totaling $9,694,714.

Disclosure enforcement - Schwab's advisory brochure (published 2026-10-15) discloses a June 2022 SEC settlement over false and misleading Form ADV Part 2A statements about cash allocations in Schwab Intelligent Portfolios.

DOL fiduciary rule vacated - Schwab's 2Q 2026 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) states that in March 2026 federal district courts vacated the DOL's April 2024 fiduciary rule and the DOL removed it from the Code of Federal Regulations.

Outlook: transparency and unbundling rather than blanket cuts - an April 2026 McKinsey report (published 2026-04-08) expects fee pressure to manifest as 'demands for transparency and unbundled pricing rather than a blanket reduction in basis points.'

claims.text: Research - Cerulli (published October 2025): The Cerulli estimate finds that while older investors tend to be more advisor-reliant, younger investors prefer to retain a greater degree of control of at least part of their investing lives; it also estimates Millennials will inherit $46 trillion over 2024-2048, more than Generation X households, while Gen X stands to inherit the greatest portion in the next 10 years ($14 trillion vs Millennials' $8 trillion).

Research - Bank of America Private Bank 2026 Study (June 2026): The 2026 Study of Wealthy Americans reports that 47% of young investors use AI to research companies or markets, 87% are comfortable with advisors using AI to help manage portfolios, yet 65% still prefer to receive investment advice from a human advisor.

Research - Bank of America Private Bank 2026 Study (June 2026): The same 2026 study reports that 42% of younger respondents own art (and 75% of non-owners are interested in owning art), and shows Gen Z/Millennials allocate 32% of their portfolio to stocks versus 58% for Gen X/Baby Boomers.

Research - Bank of America Private Bank 2024 Study (June 2024): The 2024 Study of Wealthy Americans found Millennials and Gen Z allocate three times more of their investment portfolios to alternative investments than older generations and are looking beyond traditional stock and bond markets, driving demand for investment real estate, private equity, digital assets and gold; among the 21-43 age group, 31% named real estate investments, 28% crypto/digital assets, 26% private equity and 21% companies focused on positive impact among the greatest opportunities for growth.

Peer context - Schwab (3Q25 earnings call, October 2025): Schwab CEO Rick Wurster said industry research shows Gen Z is 45% more likely to start investing by the age of 21 as compared to Millennials, that nearly one-third of new-to-firm retail households at Schwab are Gen Zers (investors between the ages of 13 and 28), and that these investors learn about finances primarily through social media and family.

Peer context - Schwab (3Q26 earnings call, October 2026): Schwab CEO Richard Wurster said approximately 70% of new-to-firm retail households are Gen Z and millennials, and that Schwab's retention rate around wealth transfers is extremely high.

Edward Jones (2025 10-K, Item 1A): Edward Jones states its continued ability to compete and adapt may be adversely impacted by generational wealth transfer, including changing client expectations for expanded product offerings and technology needs, and changing client demographics, preferences and values.

Edward Jones (2025 10-K, Item 1A): The firm describes a 'new digital platform, focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors' as one of its initiatives targeting new clients, alongside High Net Worth and Workplace initiatives, plus recently launched Financial Planning Services.

Edward Jones (2025 10-K, Item 1): The firm states its branch office model is designed to serve clients through deep, personal relationships and comprehensive advice and planning with financial advisors and CSTPs, and that it offers investment advisory programs, brokerage and retirement accounts, cash and lending solutions and financial planning offerings.

Edward Jones (2025 10-K, Item 1): The firm states its Wealth Management and Field Management division supports branch teams by helping clients achieve their financial goals through planning, advice, products and services and aims to understand the needs of clients and investors.

Technology - trade press (August 2026): InvestmentNews/Kitces trade press reports Edward Jones announced a minority stake in the personal finance app Quicken, with the stated intention of integrating Quicken's personal financial management capabilities into Edward Jones to support its value proposition and advisor conversations with clients, though Edward Jones notes it is still determining the actual deployment strategy.

Edward Jones (2025 10-K, Item 10): The firm states it seeks to address its strategic risks—most notably competition for clients and personnel in light of the evolving financial services industry and generational wealth transfer, changing client demographics, preferences and values, technology, artificial intelligence and regulatory changes—through its initiatives to deliver enhanced value and impact.

Edward Jones (2025 10-K, Item 1A): The firm describes initiatives to meet clients' planning, investing, saving, spending, borrowing and comprehensive needs, including a new digital platform focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors, and cautions it cannot reliably predict the timing or outcome of these initiatives.

Edward Jones (2025 10-K, Item 1A): The firm states it has engaged in significant digital initiatives to modernize its technology and expects to continue to do so, and warns that inability to enhance technology at the pace of the industry could decrease client and colleague satisfaction and retention.

Edward Jones (3Q25 10-Q): The firm describes Enterprise Reimagined as a multi-tiered initiative it believes will create more efficient operations by restructuring and reducing the size of the home office, removing redundancies, and 'adopting new capabilities, processes and technology to deliver more value and create a better client experience.'

Edward Jones (2Q25 10-Q): The firm attributes higher asset outflows, in part, to 'an aging client base and generational wealth transfers outside the firm,' alongside macroeconomic volatility, inflation and consumer spending.

Edward Jones (2025 10-K, Item 1): The firm states its Business Resource Groups help 'attract and retain talent and discover ways to serve clients and future clients more deeply, especially as demographics and needs change.'
Edward Jones (2Q25 10-Q): Net new households were 27,000 in 2Q25 (down from 60,000 in 2Q24) and 77,000 in the first half of 2025 (down from 124,000), with 6.7 million client households at period end.

Edward Jones (3Q25 10-Q): Net new households were 24,000 in 3Q25 (down from 53,000 in 3Q24) and 101,000 in the first nine months of 2025 (down from 177,000), with 6.7 million client households at period end.

Edward Jones (2025 10-K, Item 7): Total households were 6,546 thousand at year-end 2025 (versus 6,402 thousand in 2024 and 6,158 thousand in 2023); net new assets were $71.8 billion in 2025 (versus $71.9 billion in 2024 and $94.3 billion in 2023).
Edward Jones (1Q26 10-Q): Client households were 6.8 million at period end (up 3% from 6.6 million) and net new assets were $18 billion for the quarter (up 4% from $17 billion).

Edward Jones (2Q26 10-Q): Net new assets were $18 billion in 2Q26 (up 6% from $17 billion) and $36 billion in the first half of 2026 (up 6% from $34 billion); U.S. client households were 6.1 million at period end (up 2% from 6.0 million).

The evidence above only provides objective context for the strategic question asked. Whether or how Edward Jones should act is a judgment for the strategy team to make, beyond the scope of this evidence engine.

claims.text: The 2025 FINRA Foundation investor study (published 2025-12-04) found word of mouth from friends, family, and colleagues is the most frequently mentioned source of investment information among investors under 35, used by 85 percent, and that younger investors are somewhat less likely than older investors to rely on financial professionals.

On Schwab's 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab is "meeting them in the channels where they turn for information about investing" and that management knows Gen Z "learn about finances primarily through social media and family."
On the same 3Q25 call, management said younger investors' top online resource is YouTube, and Schwab is "the number one financial services firm on YouTube by followers."

A 2025 WealthTender advisor-search survey (published 2025-08-13; not age-segmented in the excerpt) found 96% of surveyed people would still research an advisor even if that advisor came highly recommended, and reported referrals from professionals (49.20%) and financial institutions (49.00%) as among the most-cited channels, followed by online advisor directories/matching services (31.80%), AI search tools (25.40%), and social media (22.20%).

A 2025 WealthTender advisor-search survey (published 2025-08-13; not age-segmented in the excerpt) found 73% of people consider fee transparency the most important trust factor, 48% rank pricing as the top factor in final advisor selection, and 63% consider professional credentials like CFP or CFA a key factor in determining trustworthiness; 38% identified lack of fee transparency as a red flag.

A June 2025 CFPB survey (published 2025-06-06) found people are most likely to have confidence in financial information from a qualified and competent financial advisor such as a CFP professional, and three in four Americans are comfortable acting on advice from a financial advisor without verifying it elsewhere.

The 2026 Bank of America Private Bank Study of Wealthy Americans (published 2026-06-17) found 65% of young investors still prefer to receive investment advice from a human advisor, even though 87% are comfortable with advisors using AI to help manage portfolios and 47% use AI to research companies or markets; the study defines younger investors as Gen Z and Millennials, ages 21 to 45.

The 2025 Cerulli wealth-transfer report (published 2025-10-29) states that while older investors tend to be more advisor-reliant, younger investors prefer to retain a greater degree of control of at least part of their investing lives.
A June 2025 CFPB survey (published 2025-06-06) found Millennials and members of Gen Z are more likely than older Americans to seek financial information from Instagram, X, and TikTok.
The same June 2025 CFPB survey found those aged 25-45 are more trusting than older Americans aged 46-64 of financial information from generative AI tools (44% vs. 26%) and social media (44% vs. 24%).

The 2025 FINRA Foundation investor study (published 2025-12-04) found that among investors who purchased meme stocks or other viral investments, 78% rely on investments displayed on their mobile trading app and 69% on social media groups.
Schwab's 2026 investor day deck (published 2026-05-14) lists "Build brand awareness & education with influencer-led content on TikTok, Meta, Instagram, & Reddit."

On Schwab's 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), CEO Rick Wurster said "We're all over TikTok and Instagram, and we're the most followed financial services company on YouTube," describing going where younger investors are.

A 2025 Goldman Sachs Alternatives survey (published 2025-10-17) found financial media leads as the most common information source for individual investors, followed by advisors, and that Millennials cite social media more often while Boomers rely on traditional outlets.

A 2026 FINRA Foundation finfluencer report (published 2026-04-01) found that among investors (all ages) who reported losing money to fraud, the most cited social media channels were YouTube (79%), TikTok (70%), and Instagram (67%).

Wealth transfer (size/timing/demographics) - Research: Cerulli's report (October 2025) states the Great Wealth Transfer is 'in full swing,' with trillions of dollars already changing hands annually, and warns that differences in service preferences among women and next-generation clients are likely to shift market share to firms best prepared to meet recipients' needs.

Wealth transfer (size/timing/demographics) - Research: UBS's next-generation report (published April 22, 2026) estimates USD 83 trillion in private wealth will change hands globally over the next two to three decades.

claims.text: Total client assets (numerator) - Morgan Stanley: The 3Q 2026 Wealth Management supplement (period September 30, 2026, published 2026-10-14) reports Wealth Management total client assets of $8,433 billion, of which advisor-led client assets were $6,631 billion and self-directed client assets were $1,802 billion.
claims.source_label: MS supplement - Wealth Management segment 2026-09-30, p.8 [IR]

claims.text: Total client assets (numerator) - The Charles Schwab Corporation: The 3Q 2026 press release (published 2026-10-15) reports total client assets increased 15% year-over-year to $13.33 trillion at September 30, 2026.

Total client assets (numerator) - Edward Jones: The 2Q 2026 10-Q (period ended June 26, 2026) reports the Partnership ended the quarter with $2.6 trillion of assets under care ('AUC'), including $1.2 trillion of advisory programs AUC.

Total client assets (numerator) - Merrill: The 3Q 2026 GWIM key indicators supplement (published 2026-10-14) reports Merrill Wealth Management client balances of $4,240,601 million at period end, within total GWIM client balances of $5,056,787 million.

Total client assets (numerator) - Raymond James: The fiscal 3Q 2026 press release (period June 30, 2026, published 2026-07-22) reports client assets under administration of $1,922.4 billion, of which Private Client Group assets under administration were $1,856.5 billion.
claims.source_label: RJF press - Private Client Group segment 2026-06-30 [filing]

claims.text: Advisor headcount (denominator) - Morgan Stanley: The 4Q 2020 Wealth Management supplement (published 2021-01-20) reports Wealth Management representatives of 15,950 at December 31, 2020.
Advisor headcount (denominator) - Edward Jones: The 2Q 2026 10-Q (period ended June 26, 2026) reports the Partnership ended the quarter with 20,514 financial advisors.

Advisor headcount (denominator) - Raymond James: The 2025 10-K (period ended September 30, 2025) reports 8,943 employee and independent contractor financial advisors affiliated with the firm as of September 30, 2025.

Definitions and comparability - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K defines Wealth Management client assets as those 'for which Wealth Management is providing services including financial advisor-led brokerage, investment advisory, custody, cash management, and administrative services; self-directed brokerage and investment advisory services; financial and wealth planning services; workplace services, including stock plan administration, and retirement plan services.'

Definitions and comparability - Morgan Stanley: The 3Q 2026 supplement defines advisor-led client assets as 'client assets in accounts that have a Wealth Management representative assigned' and self-directed client assets as 'active accounts which are not advisor-led,' with active accounts defined as having at least $25 in assets.

Definitions and comparability - The Charles Schwab Corporation: The 2025 10-K defines client assets as 'the market value, as of the end of the reporting period, of all client assets in our custody, BDA balances, and proprietary products, which includes both cash and securities.'

Definitions and comparability - The Charles Schwab Corporation: The 2025 10-K describes Schwab's two reportable segments as Investor Services and Advisor Services, with Advisor Services providing custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent RIAs, independent retirement advisors, and recordkeepers.
Definitions and comparability - Edward Jones: The 2Q 2026 10-Q shows the firmwide 20,514-advisor count spans U.S. financial advisors of 19,647 and Canada financial advisors of 867 at period end.

Definitions and comparability - Edward Jones: The 3Q 2025 10-Q defines attrition % as 'the annualized number of financial advisors that left or retired from the Partnership during the period compared to the total number of financial advisors as of period end.'
Definitions and comparability - Merrill: The 2Q 2026 10-Q states GWIM consists of two primary businesses: Merrill Wealth Management and Bank of America Private Bank.

Definitions and comparability - Merrill: The 2025 10-K describes Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business as providing 'a high-touch client experience through a network of financial advisors focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets.'

Definitions and comparability - Merrill: The 2025 10-K's client balances by type table shows total client balances are composed of assets under management, brokerage and other assets, deposits, and loans and leases, less managed deposits in assets under management.

Definitions and comparability - Raymond James: The 2025 10-K states financial advisors 'primarily affiliate with us directly as either employees or independent contractors or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors ('RIAs') and broker-dealers to which we provide services through our RIA and Custody Services ('RCS') division.'

Definitions and comparability - Raymond James: The 2025 10-K states 'Advisors in our RCS division are not included in our financial advisor metric although their client assets are included in PCG AUA,' and reports AUA associated with firms in the RCS division of $217.3 billion as of September 30, 2025.
claims.source_label: RJF 10-K 2025-09-30 [filing]; RJF 10-K - Private Client Group segment 2025-09-30 [filing]

parts.text: What has each of Morgan Stanley, Charles Schwab, Edward Jones, Merrill, and Raymond James disclosed about their advisor compensation structures?
parts.keyword_query: advisor compensation structure payout grid commission fee-based salary bonus incentive deferred retention award transition recruiting compensation plan advisor pay adviser compensation

claims.text: Advisor compensation structures - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K states compensation and benefits expenses include base salaries and fixed allowances, formulaic programs, discretionary incentive compensation, amortization of deferred cash and equity awards, and other items, and it attributes the 2025 increase primarily to "an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors" on higher revenues.

Advisor compensation structures - Morgan Stanley: The 2Q26 10-Q states that in the first quarter of 2026 the Firm reduced the amount of deferred compensation as a proportion of total compensation for Wealth Management advisors.

Advisor compensation structures - Morgan Stanley: The Form ADV (published 2026-11-04) discloses that the fee a client pays is a factor used in calculating the Financial Advisor's compensation; if the fee rate is below a certain threshold, the advisor receives credit for less than the total fee; and a Morgan Stanley Virtual Advisor is paid a base salary plus a discretionary bonus and does not retain any portion of the Morgan Stanley Advisory Fee.

Advisor compensation structures - Charles Schwab: Schwab's 2026 investor-day materials (published 2026-05-14) state that Schwab Advisor Network advisors are independent and are not employees or agents of Schwab, and that advisors pay fees to Schwab in connection with referrals.

Advisor compensation structures - Charles Schwab: Schwab's 3Q26 earnings deck (published 2026-10-15) states the company uses adjusted diluted EPS and return on tangible common equity as components of performance criteria for employee bonus and certain executive management incentive compensation arrangements.
Advisor compensation structures - Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K risk factors note that a significant portion of financial advisors' compensation is variable based on the Partnership's profitability.

Advisor compensation structures - Edward Jones: The Form ADV (published 2026-03-27) discloses that the Program Fee, assets under care, and Reserve Line Advance balances will impact most financial advisors' eligibility for a bonus and bonus amount, and may also impact eligibility for certain limited partnership profits interest; most financial advisors are eligible for a Travel Award based on the amount of new and existing assets under care.

Advisor compensation structures - Edward Jones: The same Form ADV discloses that a financial advisor may receive compensation in connection with Reserve Line Advances depending on the profitability of the advisor's branch.

Advisor compensation structures - Edward Jones: The 2Q26 10-Q states financial advisor compensation and benefits expense increased primarily due to increases in revenues on which commissions are earned.

Advisor compensation structures - Merrill: The Form ADV (published 2026-10-30) discloses that the advisor earns compensation based on the revenue Merrill earns from the Merrill Lynch Fee, other fees and costs not covered by that fee, Sales Charges, and referrals to Affiliates, and that Merrill retains a certain percentage of the Merrill Lynch Fee.
claims.source_label: MER adv 2026-10-30, p.53 [filing]; MER adv 2026-10-30, p.32 [filing]

claims.text: Advisor compensation structures - Merrill: The Form ADV discloses that advisors who join Merrill from other firms generally receive recruitment payments—salary guarantees, upfront awards, and compensation contingent on continued employment (deferred payments, recruitment loans)—generally based to a large extent on the size of the business at their prior firm.
Advisor compensation structures - Merrill: Merrill's Advisor Development Program page (page content as of 2026-11-03) lists "base salary and unlimited earning potential."
claims.source_label: MER press page content as of 2026-11-03 [IR]

claims.text: Advisor compensation structures - Raymond James: The 2025 10-K states that compensation for employee financial advisors primarily includes a payout on revenues they generate, and such advisors also participate in the firm's employee benefit plans.
Advisor compensation structures - Raymond James: Raymond James's affiliation-options recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) lists an "81% to 90% payout" for the Corporate RIA model.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Advisor compensation structures - Raymond James: On the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said independent payouts are higher because they cover overhead costs, real estate, and health insurance, and that employee advisors have tiered payout systems where higher production moves the advisor up the payout grid.

Advisor compensation structures - Raymond James: The Form ADV (published 2026-09-14) discloses that, depending on the advisor's annual revenue generation with the firm, the advisor can receive a higher portion of the fee paid to the firm, and newly affiliated RJA advisors through the Advisor Mastery Program may receive a salary in addition to advisory fees for a period of time.

Advisor compensation structures - Raymond James: The Form ADV lists financial incentives for affiliation, including transition assistance, bonuses, deferred compensation arrangements, enhanced pay-outs, repayable business transition or working capital loans, and administrative fee reimbursements.

claims.text: WealthManagement.com trade press (published 2026-11-12) reported Raymond James will add $18.7 billion and 70 advisors to its Financial Institutions Division as an existing FID program merges with Synovus Financial Corp., expanding Pinnacle Financial Partners' relationship with Raymond James; the advisors are expected to transition in May 2027, and FID president Stephen Kruchten called it 'a significant and highly strategic expansion of our longstanding relationship with Pinnacle Financial Partners.'

WealthManagement.com trade press (published 2026-11-12) reported the firm 'recently posted record quarterly client assets and strong recruiting gains across its advisor channels, with CEO Paul Shoukry crediting flexibility in affiliation options for the growth.'

InvestmentNews trade press (published 2026-11-06) reported Raymond James & Associates welcomed Kenneth 'Ken' Killfoil, Kathleen 'K.C.' Koch and Kris Morin, who managed over $1.5 billion in client assets at PNC Private Bank, to operate as KKM Wealth Partners within Alex. Brown in Washington, D.C.

InvestmentNews trade press (published 2026-11-06) reported Ricardo Baptiste, CFP, rejoined Ameriprise Financial in Plantation, Florida, after a six-year stint at Raymond James, returning to Ameriprise with $193 million in client assets under his practice, Wealth Investment Group.

InvestmentNews trade press (published 2026-11-05) reported Samuel 'Sam' Mintz and Stephen 'Steve' Gow joined Raymond James & Associates as managing directors from Truist Investment Services, adding more than $1.2 billion in client assets through the Mintz & Gow Group of Raymond James in Richmond, Virginia.

InvestmentNews trade press (published 2026-11-05) reported Raymond James ended its fiscal year with a record 8,943 advisors, a 2% increase year-over-year, and signaled it expects continued momentum with 'healthy pipelines of advisor commitments heading into the coming year.'

WealthManagement.com trade press (published 2026-11-05) reported Raymond James said it recruited $538 million in trailing 12-month production for advisors entering its domestic independent contractor and employee channels during the fiscal year, up from $407 million in the prior year, with those advisors representing more than $82 billion in client assets.

InvestmentNews trade press (published 2026-11-04) reported Raymond James & Associates welcomed a four-person team from UBS Financial Services that managed more than $700 million in client assets, operating as 42° North Advisors of Raymond James in Beachwood, Ohio; the publication noted the hire 'extends a consistent run of Raymond James & Associates recruiting from UBS throughout 2026.'

WealthManagement.com trade press (published 2026-10-29) reported Raymond James's fiscal fourth-quarter results: record quarter-end client assets under administration of $1.87 trillion, up 1% sequentially and 12% year-over-year; Private Client Group record quarterly net revenue of $3.06 billion, up 15% year-over-year, and pre-tax income of $458 million, up 10% year-over-year; domestic PCG net new assets up 88% for the fiscal year to a record of more than $98 billion, with quarterly net new assets of nearly $23 billion and annualized growth of 5.3% from the beginning of the quarter; and non-GAAP earnings per share of $3.59 (beating analysts' expectations by $0.32, per Seeking Alpha) on revenue of $4.74 billion, up 13% year-over-year.
WealthManagement.com trade press (published 2026-10-29) reported Raymond James no longer reports advisor headcount, but had about 8,900 advisors the last time headcount was officially broken out.

WealthManagement.com trade press (published 2026-10-29) reported that, when asked about M&A, CEO Paul Shoukry said the firm looks for acquisitions in the wealth management business in particular but they would have to be a good cultural and strategic fit: 'We don't do acquisitions to slash costs...
